Thierno Barry scored three goals and set up the other as Everton sauntered into the third round of the Carabao Cup by way of a 4-0 win over Preston at Deepdale.

The French striker scored eight goals in 41 games in 2025/26 and, after his first of the season in Saturday's Premier League win over Crystal Palace, is now already halfway to matching that total despite having played 38 games fewer.

The Toffees - who have not progressed past the third round since 2023/24 - have been drawn to face Wolves in the next round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thierno Barry completes his hat-trick for Everton as they storm past Preston in their Carabao Cup clash

A strong Everton team were in control from the off. They dominated the ball and chances came thick and fast against a Preston side who've lost two from two in the Sky Bet Championship but, for the most part, those openings were of low quality.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thierno Barry opens the scoring for Everton away to Preston in their Carabao Cup clash

The 10th attempt was a successful one. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's floated ball released Vitalii Mykolenko on the left, who laid the ball on a plate for Barry to sweep in a tidy finish.

There was a feeling the floodgates might open after that, but they didn't, so when the second half began, Preston had the bit between their teeth, which the crowd sensed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thierno Barry scores his second to double Everton's lead in their Carabao Cup clash with Preston

However, Barry's second just before the hour made the comeback less likely, and his simple finish to complete his hat-trick essentially secured Everton's progression with 20 minutes to play.

There was time for Brennan Johnson to add shine to the result, with the Welshman - who joined from Crystal Palace earlier this month - netting his first goal since November 2025 to make it 4-0.

25: GOAL ! After nine previous attempts, Barry finishes off a slick move to put Everton in front.

! Iliman Ndiaye tees up Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, whose cross is pushed straight into the path of Barry, who makes no mistake. 65: SAVE ! Jordan Pickford makes his only significant save of the night to keep out a sweetly-struck overhead kick from Callum Lang.

! Jordan Pickford makes his only significant save of the night to keep out a sweetly-struck overhead kick from Callum Lang. 70: GOAL ! Dewsbury-Hall finds substitute Johnson, who gains a yard on Lewis Gibson and squares for Barry, who sweeps in to complete his hat-trick.

! Dewsbury-Hall finds substitute Johnson, who gains a yard on Lewis Gibson and squares for Barry, who sweeps in to complete his hat-trick. 72: GOAL! Barry turns provider, laying a beautiful ball off for Johnson, who arrives in a similar position, but this time goes alone to add the gloss.

Heckingbottom: The second goal changed the game

Preston's Paul Heckingbottom speaking on Sky Sports Football:

"It's just frustrating we were going to make the subs and they scored the (second) goal as we had them all lined up. It just changed the game. The goals after that were disappointing

"We were playing against top opposition, we know that, but one or two things, fundamentally, don't help you keep clean sheets anyway. It doesn't matter who you are playing against.

"Because of where we are at the minute, it's hard to take the pressure off the defenders as we've not got attacking changes. We've got defenders on the bench, a couple more midfielders, wing-backs and some young boys. That's where we're at; we need attacking changes so we can keep the pressure on. And that's a problem for us at the minute."

Moyes discusses progression, Barry and Johnson

Everton's David Moyes speaking on Sky Sports Football:

"It ended up being a little bit more comfortable than I thought it might have been before the game, but it's a really good result for us.

"I thought we played well at times and our football was quite good, but we need to finish things off a bit better in the first half than we did, but I'm really pleased we scored four goals."

On Thierno Barry: "I told him [at the end of last season] he has to do a lot better than he did before. That's it. We want centre-forwards to score goals. I don't think it's easy for anybody coming to the Premier League in their first season, especially centre-forwards. He'll learn a lot more, he'll see a lot more and he's come in with a much better attitude generally, so whoever's working with him is doing a good job."

On Brennan Johnson: "We want to find what he did at Tottenham when he was scoring all those goals. His assist tonight was brilliant and his finish as well. People who've watched Brennan over the years will tell you that looks a bit more like him. We don't want to bring him on too quick, but he's done well tonight."

Sports.title: Barnes double fires Newcastle past West Brom
Sports.content:
Harvey Barnes struck twice for Newcastle as they survived a scare against West Brom to win 3-2 and reach the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Isaac Price's first-half free-kick gave the Baggies a surprise lead at St James' Park, as he evaded Ewen Jaouen in the Newcastle goal with a smart effort on his debut for the club.

Another debutant then levelled for the Magpies, as Bazoumana Toure poked in from close range, awarded the goal after there was some uncertainty over whether it was he or West Brom defender Chris Mepham who got the final touch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Gonzalez is brought out at St. James' Park to the Newcastle fans after it was announced he has signed from Manchester City.

Newcastle draw Millwall in third round Newcastle will face Millwall in the third round of the Carabao Cup at The Den. The fixture will take place either w/c Mon Sep 7, or w/c Mon Sep 14.

Barnes was then introduced at half-time for Toure, and swiftly completed the turnaround to put Newcastle ahead, firing in from close range after his initial effort from the edge of the box was blocked.

The pendulum would swing again, as Lewis Hall gave away another penalty - following on from the spot-kick he conceded to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday - which Price stepped up to convert and make it 2-2.

But several minutes later Barnes found the winner, sweeping in from close range to put Newcastle into the draw for the competition they won in 2025.

The key moments from Newcastle's second-round victory

19: GOAL! How about that?! A free-kick about 25 yards out... it looks like Isaac Price is going to whip a cross in, but instead he decides to sneak one around the wall and into the bottom corner. Jaouen completely flummoxed in the Newcastle goal!

38: GOAL! On his debut! Newcastle had been creeping back into the game and now they've found the equaliser! Steur works it wide to Amar Dedic. He then fizzes a ball into the middle and Toure looks to have stolen in to slot in.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harvey Barnes restores Newcastle's lead over West Brom in their Carabao Cup clash.

48: GOAL! Off the bench and in amongst the goals right away! Barnes puts Newcastle ahead. A corner comes to Barnes on the edge of the box. He drives a shot low in towards goal that West Brom can't properly clear. And the winger has followed his shot into the box and he's on hand to then fire into the net!

76: PENALTY TO WEST BROM! Hall again! A handball from the Newcastle left-back and he's given away another spot-kick... just as he did against Liverpool on Sunday! West Brom have the chance to level!

77: GOAL! Price sends the Jaouen the wrong way! West Brom are level!!

81: GOAL! Lead restored! Barnes again! Anthony Elanga bursts down the right and then tees a pass into Dedic. He crosses low into the middle and Barnes finishes first time in the middle.

Jaissle praises Barnes after victory

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle:

"It's not only goals. As we saw also against Liverpool he was doing a really great job, not only in possession, also out of possession.

"He is disciplined, especially also with the combination with (Lewis) Hall. We're really pleased, I thanked him after the match, it was important that he scored."

Jaissle was full of praise for Championship side West Brom, revealing he spoke to opposite number James Morrison after the game.

"Relieved, it's always the most important thing in a Cup run that you take the result, that's what we did against a strong opponent.

"I had a chat with the gaffer. They're doing really well, I think they will play a great role in the Championship.

"But we also responded. It was important we saw character on the pitch, also after the second equaliser we stepped back and straight away we scored, that helped us of course.

"We are happy, an entertaining match for the fans. I think I would have less (of a) headache if we had not conceded the penalties."

Redknapp impressed by Jaissle in early stages of Newcastle tenure

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp says everyone needs to stay calm with the new Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle.

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp:

"He's done well so far.

"It's early days. He probably thought it was a really good job for him and a great opportunity. It's difficult at the moment, but Nico Gonzalez will be a good signing for them in that No 6.

"They had that midfield that had been so formidable in Guimaraes, Tonali and Joelinton and obviously it's all changed now.

"He's got a lot of young players and a little bit of pace. You could say he's already got more out of Yoane Wissa and Anthony Elanga than Eddie Howe did, even after just that one game against Liverpool.

"They're going to be all right, Newcastle. Everyone just has to stay calm with the manager and they'll get some good results."

Sports.title: Police investigating alleged assault in connection with Carse nightclub incident
Sports.content:
Derbyshire Police said on Wednesday it was investigating allegations of an assault in the city centre, but no arrests have yet been made

Brydon Carse has been dropped from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan

Derbyshire Police are looking into "allegations of assault" following the incident that saw England bowler Brydon Carse handcuffed outside a nightspot over the weekend.

Carse was removed from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan, which begins at Lord's on Thursday morning, after the Cricket Regulator initiated a probe into an episode that saw the Durham player briefly arrested outside a late bar in Derby - then de-arrested after agreeing to depart.

In an updated statement issued on Wednesday evening, Derbyshire Police said: "We are investigating allegations of assault in Derby city centre. No arrests have yet been made and the investigation is ongoing."

Further details are unknown, with no clarity over what part - if any - Carse had in the alleged assault.

The England and Wales Cricket Board declined to comment when contacted by the Press Association.

An initial statement from the force, released after a video clip of Carse apparently being detained by officers in the street, had said: "A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night. However the man was de-arrested shortly afterwards having agreed to leave the area."

Former England captain Ben Stokes and centrally contracted seamer Matthew Potts both appeared in the footage, captured in the aftermath of their Durham's side's County Championship victory over Derbyshire, though there is no suggestion that either was involved in anything untoward.

Reacting to the incident, Stokes' replacement as Test skipper Joe Root spoke angrily about the latest in a growing line of alcohol-related issues which have swamped the team.

Root, who made a point of abolishing the midnight curfew which played a partial role in Stokes' exit following another controversial night out earlier this summer, said: "If I'm being brutally honest I'm really hacked off.

"I've spoken to Brydon and when I first found out my first concern was him as a person. I don't think I'm speaking out of turn in saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.

"But it's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact we continuously keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we are doing on the field."

Sports.title: 'All-time great status awaits Mayer vs Cameron winner'
Sports.content:
The winner of Mikaela Mayer and Chantelle Cameron's world title unification fight will cement their position as one of the top five female fighters in boxing history, according to Nakisa Bidarian.

The WBO, WBA and WBC titles are on the line when Mayer and Cameron headline MVPW-06 at Birmingham's BP Pulse LIVE Arena this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

Bidarian, CEO of Most Valuable Promotions, believes Cameron is already in the conversation to be one of the greatest women's boxers by virtue of beating Katie Taylor in their epic two-fight rivalry in 2023.

"The winner cements themselves as one of the top five fighters in history," Bidarian told Sky Sports.

"Chantelle Cameron has to be considered one of the GOATs because she beat Katie Taylor, and she almost beat Katie Taylor a second time, and Katie Taylor undoubtedly is one of the GOATs of women's boxing.

"If Mikaela Mayer can go in there and beat Chantelle Cameron decisively, she'll be one of the GOATs.

"But Cameron is already one of the greatest of all time and whatever time she has left in her career, she's going to be one of the faces of the sport alongside Mikaela as well."

Mayer vs Cameron - fighter records

Mikaela Mayer Wins 22 Losses 2

Chantelle Cameron Wins 22 Losses 1

A new era of women's boxing

With Taylor one farewell fight away from bringing the curtain down on her illustrious boxing career, and rival Amanda Serrano chasing the women's knockout record and a 50th career victory before hanging up her gloves, a vacancy as the face of women's boxing could soon emerge.

But, aged 36 and 35 respectively, Bidarian believes the baton will be passed to someone else featuring on Saturday's fight card.

"When I think about the future, when Amanda and Katie transition into the next phase of their personal lives and professional careers," Bidarian added.

"We have other fighters on this card that are going to represent that movement, starting with Caroline Dubois."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caroline Dubois is determined to fight rival Alycia Baumgardner sooner rather than later

Britain's Dubois looks to retain her WBC and WBO lightweight titles against unbeaten former US Olympian Amelia Moore in the co-main event of MVPW-06 in Birmingham.

Alycia Baumgardner, a long-time rival and potential future opponent of Dubois, is set to be in attendance at ringside, but Bidarian has urged the 25-year-old to focus on matters inside the ring.

"It's going to be a very exciting fight week and fight night," Bidarian said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alycia Baumgardner dismissed the prospects of facing Caroline Dubois after her win over Bo Mi Re Shin. Instead, the fighter called out Katie Taylor and Amanda Serrano

"Alycia Baumgardner will be there, but Caroline has a very formidable opponent ahead of her. You cannot discount Amelia Moore just because she's 4-0.

"She has a rich amateur pedigree. She's also competed in Team Combat League, which is a different boxing product in the US, and she's a strong athlete.

"I'm focused on what happens on fight night. I think it's an absolute challenge for Caroline. It'll be interesting to see what version of Caroline Dubois we get."

Sports.title: Sávio savours debut goal as Spurs coast to emphatic Carabao Cup win over Charlton
Sports.content:
A new season at the snazziest modern stadium in England and something extremely welcome for Tottenham. A home win over domestic opposition. There were only four of them last time out; three in the Premier League with the final one – over Everton on the last day – helping them to avoid relegation. Had they lost that, this Carabao Cup fixture against Charlton would also have been played in the Championship.

Spurs needed this tonic for another reason – to begin the clean-up operation after Saturday’s awful 3-0 defeat at Brentford.

The season could not have started any worse. With no European football, a decent cup run or runs are imperative and Spurs got themselves up and running in this competition on a night when everything came together perfectly.

For a good while, it looked as though Mikey Moore was going to be the story.

The homegrown 19-year-old broke the deadlock with a vicious drive from the edge of the area; it was the purity of the strike that made it. But then came Sávio.

Spurs were 3-0 up with further goals from Dominic Solanke and the substitute, Kevin Danso, when Roberto De Zerbi sent on his £75m signing from Manchester City for his debut. It was a devastating cameo from Sávio, something to wet the whistle for the bigger challenges ahead. “A perfect day for him,” De Zerbi said.

It took Sávio just 11 minutes to score and it was a lovely goal – a glide inside from the right, his markers close and yet nowhere near, his control of the situation total before the fizzing low finish into the near corner. De Zerbi has said he wants end product from Sávio, especially goals and he challenged him afterwards to score 10-12 before the end of the season. This was a good start. There was more.

Once again, it was Sávio on the right, cutting back, closer to goal this time. He put one would-be challenger down and skated around another. It was all about the composure. The shot hit his teammate, Ben Davies, and went in. The goal was credited to Davies, who was pretty unapologetic about it.

The Charlton manager, Nathan Jones, made wholesale changes to his preferred lineup – 10 in total from Saturday’s win at West Ham – and it was a difficult evening for his team. “Absolutely disastrous,” as he put it. “This was a game we didn’t need.” Charlton did enjoy the last word when another substitute, Lloyd Jones, headed home from a corner.

View image in fullscreen Mikey Moore of Tottenham Hotspur scored their first goal. Photograph: Elli Birch/IPS/Shutterstock

The major take-away was the sense of possibility brought by Sávio, with De Zerbi insisting he was not daunted by being drawn to face Liverpool at Anfield in the next round. “It’s a great game,” he said. “If we want to win the competition, we have to win these games.”

It was a night when there was a focus on De Zerbi’s selection. There was a sense of the cavalry returning. The manager started Destiny Udogie, Rodrigo Bentancur, Mateus Fernandes and Solanke, players that were fit enough only for the bench at Brentford. Pedro Porro and Micky van de Ven, who did not kick a ball in pre-season and were not available for Brentford, were among the substitutes. They got on. There was no Marcos Senesi or Sandro Tonali in the squad. They will be ready for Newcastle here on Saturday.

Thank you for your feedback.

Spurs were always going to dominate the ball. The question concerned what they could create with it. The answer at the outset was very little. Spurs did not threaten until the 30th minute when Solanke had a shot blocked and Archie Gray extended the goalkeeper, Tiernan Brooks, with a low prod on the rebound. Charlton might have been in front by then. Greg Docherty exploded a drive through a crowd that Antonin Kinsky did well to save while Nathan Asiimwe headed narrowly off target.

Spurs upped the tempo after the Brooks save from Gray. Fernandes impressed. There was a flicker from Moore, even if the end product was not there. Then it was. Gloriously. When Moore moved inside from the right, the Charlton player close to him – Millenic Alli – slipped. Moore knew what he had to do and the sweetness of the left-footed connection took the breath. The shot ripped through the hands of Brooks.

View image in fullscreen Dominic Solanke displays textbook technique to double Tottenham’s advantage. Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty Images

What Charlton did not need shortly afterwards was hesitant defending inside their box on a bouncing ball. Lucas Bergvall saw a shot blocked and Timothy Ouma seemed to freeze. When it broke for Solanke, he swept a clinical finish into the bottom corner.

Moore’s only other goal for Spurs was against Elfsborg in the Europa League in January 2025. After that game, his teammate, James Maddison, compared him to Neymar. Moore’s career trajectory has not been as steep as once envisaged but he remains young. He wanted to do more in the second half and there was a swagger about him on the ball; some lovely skills and darting runs. The home crowd saluted him. He remains a loan target for FC Köln before the transfer window shuts. As De Zerbi acknowledged, he needs regular football.

De Zerbi introduced Porro, van de Ven and Danso after Gray had once again worked Brooks. It was some entrance from Danso, his first touch a header past Brooks from Fernandes’ free-kick. He was bloodied into the bargain, caught in the aerial challenge by the Charlton substitute, Danny McNamara. Sávio stood and watched. He was stripped and ready while Danso had treatment. He had to wait. When he got on, he more than made his mark.

Sports.title: Barnes settles stormer to hand Jaissle first Newcastle win against West Brom
Sports.content:
Around this time last week Matthias Jaissle wore a sorrowful look as he spoke of his “disappointment” at the “negativity” surrounding a transitional young Newcastle side.

Fast forward seven days and a team slightly unlucky to have been held to a draw at home by Liverpool last Sunday have now provided Jaissle with his first competitive win since replacing Eddie Howe as head coach. It is safe to say the doubters are being confounded.

Granted Newcastle’s passage to the third round of the Carabao Cup and an impending visit to Millwall was not exactly seamless against a very decent West Brom but it appears that Jaissle’s faith is far from groundless.

It helps that he has been able to sign the £30m right-back Amar Dedic from Benfica. Dedic, who played for the German at RB Salzburg, shone here with his stellar crosses creating one of Harvey Barnes’s two goals and another for Bazoumana Touré.

“West Brom were a strong opponent, they’re brave and I will follow them now but I’m happy,” said Jaissle, who delighted home supporters by engaging in an animated stoppage-time debate with match officials over a disputed free-kick. “Amar joined us late but it’s like he’s been here for years.”

Ten minutes before kick-off Nico González, Newcastle’s £52m signing from Manchester City, was introduced to the crowd. As the stadium echoed to chants of “Nico, Nico,” the Spanish holding midfielder beamed broadly.

View image in fullscreen Harvey Barnes sweeps the ball home to score Newcastle’s third goal. Photograph: Richard Lee/Shutterstock

When González’s new head coach first talked to Newcastle executives about succeeding Howe at the end of July, part of their pitch involved a spot of modern Geordie history. Jaissle was shown a video of 300,000 fans packing the city centre as Howe’s team brought the 2025 Carabao Cup back to Tyneside. “They tried to convince me with that footage,” he said. “But it was not needed.”

The German’s hopes of lifting the trophy himself next spring were initially dented as West Brom took a 19th-minute lead.

With the visiting Ousmane Diakité establishing himself as a key central midfield combatant, the Championship side grew increasingly confident. When they won a free-kick, Isaac Price curled that 25-yard dead ball around the wall and beat Ewen Jaouen at his near post.

Jaissle’s second-choice goalkeeper, a 20-year-old Frenchman signed from Ligue 2 Reims, got a hand to the ball and arguably should have saved it. Not that the 2,000 travelling fans perched high in the Leazes End were complaining.

James Morrison’s team impressed while winning their first two second-tier games this season and, for a while at least, his fluid version of 4-4-2 confused Newcastle and subdued Nick Woltemade in equal measure.

Then the 18-year-old Sean Steur – culpable for conceding the foul for the preceding free-kick – began re-asserting himself in the home anchoring role. The former Ajax midfielder’s fine run and pass permitted Dedic to whip in a brilliant cross that Touré lashed in from close range under considerable pressure from Chris Mepham.

View image in fullscreen Ewen Jaouen is beaten at his near post by Isaac Price’s free-kick on his Newcastle debut. Photograph: Adam Cook/IPS/Shutterstock

As Jaissle raised a celebratory fist he could reflect that three exciting recent arrivals – Steur, Dedic and Touré – had combined seamlessly for that equaliser. As Touré, a Côte d’Ivoire left winger signed from Hoffenheim to replace Anthony Gordon, celebrated his first goal for Newcastle it appeared that there really might be life at St James’ Park after Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães after all.

Touré was replaced by Barnes at the interval and the substitute wasted no time in reminding Jaissle that he is far from a shabby left winger either. Three minutes into the second half Barnes gave Newcastle the lead after pouncing on the fallout from a corner and firing the ball home from close range at the second attempt after his initial shot was blocked.

West Brom’s legs turned a little heavy but they revived when Lewis Hall handled in the area and Price registered his second goal of the night after beating Jaouen from the penalty spot.

Extra time beckoned but Barnes was not about to be eclipsed and duly swept another splendid, low Dedic cross beyond Matt Ingram.

“We were in the game, pushing Newcastle right to the end,” said Morrison. “We gave them some problems. I had a nice chat with Matthias afterwards; he was very complimentary.”

Sports.title: Thierno Barry fires hat-trick as ruthless Everton sweep Preston aside
Sports.content:
Thierno Barry resembled a striker reborn, and the goalscorer David Moyes desperately needs, as the first hat-trick of his Everton career plus an assist for new signing Brennan Johnson delivered a resounding win for the Scot on his competitive return to Preston.

The France under-21 international scored eight times in a difficult debut season in England but has half that amount two games into this fledgling campaign. Barry followed up his header against Crystal Palace with a poacher’s hat-trick to give Moyes a convincing victory back at the club where he made his name before leaving for Everton in 2002.

“Thierno worked with somebody back home in the summer who tried to change his mindset a bit,” said the Everton manager of the 23-year-old’s early season improvement. “He found it difficult last year, as a lot of boys coming in from overseas do, and it can be even worse if you’re a centre forward. Generally, he has been much better since he came back but I would still like more. A couple of his goals were laid on a plate and I want him to score some of the other opportunities he had as well.”

Before the tie Moyes attracted accusations of a lack of ambition – the kind that has contributed to the longest trophy drought in Everton’s history at 31 years – with a spiky response to being asked how important cup competitions are this season. “I’ll ask you the question,” he had replied. “Is winning a cup more important than staying in the Premier League? What would your answer be?” But a club of Everton’s stature should not have to choose between league survival and cup success. Perhaps Moyes’s question was directed towards Everton’s owners, The Friedkin Group, who have so far shown little ambition themselves in this summer’s transfer market. The Scot maintains Everton are short on numbers and quality ahead of Tuesday’s deadline.

The Everton manager could not be accused of treating the Carabao Cup lightly on the evidence of his team selection at Deepdale, where only Jarrad Branthwaite and Tyrique George were missing from the side that started on the opening day. Paul Heckingbottom, by contrast, made seven changes from the Preston team beaten by Wolves on Saturday.

View image in fullscreen Thierno Barry fires Everton into a first-half lead from Vitalii Mykolenko’s square pass. Photograph: James Harrison/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Everton’s approach mirrored Moyes’s intent. The visitors dominated from the start with Preston struggling to establish a foothold. Harrison Armstrong received a warm reception on his return to the club where he spent a fruitful spell on loan last season and, as against Palace, produced another accomplished display. The 19-year-old’s sharp touches and movement, alongside that of Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, stretched the Championship defence repeatedly.

Dewsbury-Hall engineered the breakthrough with a beautifully weighted pass over the Preston defence to Vitalii Mykolenko. The Everton left-back’s neat control gave him time to assess his options and he squared for Barry to convert with ease.

Preston’s threat was virtually non-existent in the first half. There was more aggression and less deference from the home side after the restart but, just as Deepdale found hope, Barry extinguished it with his second of the night. The rebound fell kindly for the in-rushing Barry to poke home.

Barry completed his hat-trick with a tap-in from Johnson’s selfless cross before returning the favour with a defence-splitting pass that the Everton substitute slid under the exposed Preston keeper. “I loved being back,” said Moyes of his return to Deepdale. No wonder, on this evidence.

Sports.title: Mbappé hat-trick sinks Real Sociedad after Real Madrid jeered by home fans
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappé scored a hat-trick as Real Madrid beat Real Sociedad 4-1 at the Bernabéu on Wednesday ⁠in their first home match since the return of José Mourinho as head coach.

Mbappé put Madrid ahead in the 40th minute before Luka Sucic levelled four minutes later, but the ⁠France forward restored the ⁠hosts’ lead on ​the hour. Vinícius Júnior added a third in the 68th minute before Mbappé completed his treble 10 minutes from time.

It was a winning return ⁠to the Bernabéu for Mourinho, more than 13 years after his previous home match in charge of the club, as Madrid recovered from a disjointed first half ⁠with a ruthless display after the break.

Madrid were jeered before half-time after a sluggish opening in which they ​looked short of rhythm, careless in possession and ‌vulnerable on the counterattack.

“There’s always a sense of justice in the ​boos and the applause, and the odd boo now ‌and then doesn’t do anyone any ‌harm – it helps you grow,” Mourinho said at full time. “We all know the Santiago Bernabéu and just how demanding the fans ‌are here, and I’m very pleased with how my players responded under pressure and put in a great second half, in which we could even have scored more goals.”

Real Sociedad carried ‌the sharper threat early on and almost went ahead in the 10th minute when Takefusa Kubo intercepted ‌a loose pass near the edge of the box and slipped in Mikel Oyarzabal, whose close-range effort was kept out by Thibaut Courtois.

Quick Guide Champions League: Fenerbahce stun Lyon, Viking march on Show Fenerbahce upset Lyon in the Champions League playoffs on Wednesday to advance, while Viking Stavanger joined fellow Norwegians Bodø/Glimt in the league phase with victory over Dinamo Zagreb. With the teams locked at 1-1 from the first leg in Istanbul a week ago, the Turkish giants opened up a 2-0 lead in the first half of the return fixture in France. Vedat Muriqi and English defender Archie Brown [pictured] were on target for the visitors, with winger Malick Fofana giving Lyon faint hope in the second half. Viking hit back from a goal down on the night against Dinamo Zagreb, winning 3-1 in Norway and 5-3 on aggregate. Albania's Arber Hoxha gave Dinamo an early lead but Zlatko Tripic equalised from the penalty spot just eight minutes later. Two early goals in the second half from Edvin Austbø and Tobias Moi sealed Viking’s progress to their first Champions League group phase. Barnabas Varga scored a double and former Real Madrid forward Luka Jovic added another as AEK Athens cruised into the league phase with a 4-0 thrashing of Levski Sofia. Romania's Razvan Marin added a penalty as the Greeks booked their progress following a 0-0 draw in the first leg in Bulgaria. Panama’s Cristian Martínez scored the extra-time winner for Slovan Bratislava as they overcame Slovenian champions Celje. After a 1-1 draw in the first leg, Andraz Sporar gave the Slovakians an early lead at Celje but Svit Seslar equalised fom the penalty spot, before Martínez secured a 3-2 aggregate success. The visitors went close again in the 34th minute, Sergio Gómez flashing a fine volley just wide of the far post, as the Bernabéu crowd began to voice its frustration.

Mbappé briefly changed the mood five minutes before half-time with a flash of class. Fede Valverde collected ‌the ball just beyond midfield and split the defence with a superb pass, allowing Mbappé to surge into the box, cut left and lash a shot into the top ​corner.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho was in the home dugout at the Bernabéu for the first time in 13 years. Photograph: Diego Souto/Getty Images

But Madrid’s defensive uncertainty returned four minutes later. Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen and Álvaro Carreras were all caught out after Job Ochieng latched on to a long ball, his deflected effort falling to Sucic on the right, who had time to steady himself and drill a low shot past Courtois.

Mourinho sent on Marc Cucurella at ⁠half-time and Madrid emerged transformed, with Vinícius and Mbappé stretching the visitors ​with direct running and greater intensity.

The ​hosts regained the lead on the ​hour when Mbappé and Jude Bellingham exchanged a sharp one-two, leaving the France captain ​free inside the box to ‌beat Álex Remiro ​with a low finish. Eight ​minutes later, Bellingham’s pressing won the ball back near the byline and his low cross gave Vinícius the simplest of tap-ins from close range.

Mbappé completed the win in the 80th minute after Vinícius slipped a clever pass behind the defence, the forward lifting a composed chip over Remiro to seal his hat-trick.

“This guy is incredible,” Mourinho said of Mbappé. “I see him really hungry to make history with Real Madrid, and I see a team where, despite Kylian being Kylian, it’s hard for me not to talk about the team.”

Sports.title: Chelsea in talks with Martínez’s camp as Aston Villa close on striker Jackson
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been offered Emiliano Martínez and are considering a bid for the goalkeeper. The club are in talks with Martínez’s camp, and are also braced for a bid from Manchester City for the World Cup winner’s Argentina teammate Enzo Fernández.

Martínez has told Aston Villa he wants to leave but a move to Juventus collapsed last week after Villa had signed his replacement, Zion Suzuki, from Parma for £30m.

Goalkeeper has been a problematic position for Chelsea in recent seasons, with Robert Sánchez mainly the No 1 but prone to mistakes. Mike Penders, 21, is being lined up to become the first-choice, but the Chelsea manager, Xabi Alonso, selected Sánchez for Monday’s win against Fulham when two Sánchez errors led to goals.

The availability and offer of Martínez has intrigued Chelsea and they are mulling whether it is too good an opportunity to turn down. The 33-year-old is a vastly experienced serial trophy winner. He won the World Cup in 2022 and reached the 2026 final. He also lifted the Europa League with Villa last season and the FA Cup with Arsenal in 2020.

Martínez was not in the squad for Villa’s heavy opening-weekend defeat at Brighton. Marco Bizot started in goal with Suzuki on the bench. Martínez joining Chelsea may solve a problem for both clubs.

Chelsea and Villa, meanwhile, have agreed a £65m deal for striker Nicolas Jackson to join the Midlands club. The Senegal international was also a target for Atlético Madrid but is poised to join Villa as a replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal for a £50m fee. At the start of pre-season, Villa expected to retain Martínez and Watkins but in recent weeks both signalled a desire to leave; if their departures are finalised, six of Villa’s starting XI from their Europa League triumph in May will no longer be at the club.



Villa offered Watkins a new contract but Riyadh-based Al-Hilal pursued a deal after being given encouragement that Watkins was keen on the move. He trained away from the first team as talks intensified.



Jackson will be tasked with filling the void left by Watkins, who joined Villa from Brentford for a then club-record £28m in September 2020. The 30-year-old reached double figures for goals in each of his six Premier League seasons at the club.





Jackson has been a longstanding target for Villa manager Unai Emery, who worked with the striker – who spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich – at Villarreal. “Unai taught me everything about football,” Jackson said of Emery last year.

Villa also want a centre-back and may target West Ham’s Jean-Clair Todibo.

Meanwhile, City are expected to make an offer for Fernández. Any deal would leave Chelsea seeking a replacement before Tuesday night’s transfer deadline. Chelsea previously told City to pay £120m by 14 August or miss out, but the midfielder remains a priority target for City’s manager, Enzo Maresca, who he worked with at Chelsea. Alonso started Reece James and Roméo Lavia in central midfield at Fulham, introducing Fernández from the bench.

City continued their midfield rebuild on Wednesday by buying Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a €100m (£85.7m) deal and selling Nico González to Newcastle for £52m.

Sports.title: Debutant Malard breaks Chelsea duck after Real Sociedad threaten WCL shock
Sports.content:
Chelsea’s sluggish start in the first leg of their Champions League qualifier against Real Sociedad will have made far from satisfying viewing for their suspended head coach, Sonia Bompastor, but two goals from the new signing Melvine Malard contributed to a five-goal haul as the Blues came from behind to give themselves a three-goal cushion going into next week’s return fixture.

“It was a tough game, a tough first half because Real Sociedad is a really great team but I think we had a good reaction,” said Camille Abily, the assistant coach to Bompastor, who was serving a one match ban following her red card in Chelsea’s quarter-final second leg against Arsenal last season. “We were so much better in the second half, there was more space also. It’s a good win – a tough win but a good win.”

Chelsea looked rusty at the Cherry Red Records Stadium, their new home for domestic cup competitions, with WSL fixtures being played at Stamford Bridge. A commercially focused pre-season jaunt to New Zealand and Australia perhaps did not provide the best of preparatory tests prior to this fixture.

Their sluggishness was contrasted by Real Sociedad’s sharpness and a confidence that was perhaps delivered by a strong end to their pre-season which included a 1-1 draw with the eight-time European champions OL Lyonnes.

View image in fullscreen Melvine Malard (right) is Chelsea’s impact sub off the bench, scoring twice in the second half. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

The visiting team were tenacious and well organised and opened the scoring in style when a corner was cleared to the edge of the box and the forward Ainhoa Marín, who joined from Deportivo this summer, met it unmarked, sending a looping shot in at the far post.

Despite looking far from their best, the home team drew level in the 30th minute, when Katie McCabe’s corner looked to take the smallest of touches off the captain, Naomi Girma, as it was swept in.

After the break it was a different story. Chelsea played with an energy that implied they had had the riot act read to them, or read it to themselves. They maintained their momentum despite the visiting team cancelling out Veerle Buurman’s goal from a Lauren James corner that had given them the lead for a brief four minutes.

Chelsea were a tad unlucky that Buurman’s precise sliding tackle delivered the ball to the feet of an arriving Cecilia Marcos who fired past Hannah Hampton to pull them back level. The Real Sociedad bench erupted and the goalscorer, who suffered back-to-back anterior cruciate ligament injuries in 2021 and 2023 and only fully rediscovered her form last season, was engulfed by her teammates.

View image in fullscreen Veerle Buurman rises highest to put Chelsea 2-1 up in new surroundings at AFC Wimbledon. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters

Except Chelsea had a stronger bench, greater experience and exploited the high line of the visitors to far greater effect as legs tired. It took the substitute Malard 12 minutes to make her mark on her Chelsea debut as they kept their momentum despite conceding. The France striker collected Sjoeke Nüsken’s poked through-ball, sat down a defender and waited coolly for the goalkeeper to commit before rolling the ball into the empty net.

James delivered Chelsea’s fourth and gave them a more comfortable lead when she turned in Ellie Carpenter’s ball from close range. Carpenter delivered similarly for her former Lyonnes teammate Malard to get her second as the clock ticked down to put the hosts a step closer to the league phase.

On whether it is an advantage to have these tough competitive games ahead of the start of the new domestic season next week, Abily said: “For sure. We saw we started slow. We started slow, even though we’ve played some friendly games. We also played against the boys last week. It’s not the same though, it’s not competition. It’s important to have this kind of game.”

Sports.title: Ten-man Hearts stun Rapid Vienna in shootout to reach Conference League
Sports.content:
Beau Reus made two penalty saves as heroic Hearts overcame Tomas Magnusson’s red card to pull off a stunning shootout victory away to Rapid Vienna, and book themselves a return to the Conference League’s main phase.

Following a 2-2 draw in the first leg at Tynecastle, the Jambos’ European journey looked to be fizzling out when they were reduced to 10 men in the 75th minute of the playoff round second leg, while already trailing to Ercan Kara’s first-half goal.

Substitute Landry Kaboré equalised a few minutes later before Calvin Miller volleyed 10-man Hearts ahead in the 10th minute of extra-time. Rapid hit back in the 119th minute, Nenad Cvetkovic’s goal making it 4-4 on aggregate.

But Hearts rediscovered their poise to edge the shootout 4-3 and secure what may be their most significant result in Europe for more than two decades. It means they will compete in the Conference League proper for the third time in five seasons.

The visitors suffered a blow in the 15th minute when Tom Renaud was carried off after Rapid attacker Petter Dahl fell awkwardly on his leg while being fouled by Jordi Altena. ­Magnusson replaced the Frenchman but Hearts were struggling to get a foothold early on, and the breakthrough came for Rapid in the 34th minute.

View image in fullscreen Calvin Miller finishes acrobatically to put Hearts ahead in extra time Photograph: Lukas Grinaj/SNS Group

Demir’s low shot from the right took a nick off Oisin McEntee and broke kindly to the unmarked Kara, who slotted into the empty net from six yards out. Hearts were almost handed a way back into it when Cláudio Braga seized on a loose pass but his angled shot from inside the box was beaten away by Niklas Hedl.

Hearts enjoyed a spell of pressure towards the end of the half, with Josh McPake and McEntee threatening with shots from outside the box. After the break, the Jambos captain, Blair Spittal, volleyed just wide from 20 yards out, before James Wilson and Braga both spurned opportunities.

Magnusson then sent a close-range header wide from a Spittal free-kick, but the Icelandic midfielder’s night was cut short when he was shown a second yellow card for a trip on Jannes Horn in the 76th minute.

Despite the setback, Wouter Vrancken’s side drew level within three minutes, as Kaboré adjusted his body and chested Spittal’s corner into the net at the near post, sending the game to extra time.

Remarkably, Hearts went ahead in the 100th minute when Miller acrobatically volleyed in a cross from substitute Rogers Mato. But just as the depleted Jambos looked like hanging on, Cvetkovic knocked in Moulaye Haidara’s cross in the 119th minute to force penalties.

View image in fullscreen Hearts keeper Beau Reus saves a penalty from Marco Tilio and send his side into the Conference League. Photograph: Christian Hofer/Shutterstock

Miller, Altena, Mato and Sabah Kerjota all scored from the spot for Hearts, with McEntee the only Hearts player to miss. Reus saved two kicks, denying Haidara and Marco Tilio to emerge as the hero in Vienna.

Victory brought welcome relief for Vrancken after a punishing run of European results, with his side losing 6-0 on aggregate to Sturm Graz in the Champions League qualifiers. Hearts then lost 6-1 in Lisbon and 7-2 on aggregate to Benfica in the Europa League, dropping into the Conference League playoffs as a result.

“We played a really bad first half, a little bit similar [to] Benfica. We had a game plan and we didn’t show the guts to follow up,” Vrancken told BBC Scotland. “We were already pretty angry at half-time, and we came out, we did much better. We took the game in our hands, we were dominant.”

“They have to learn that they’re a good team, that they’re good players, that they can show it and show the guts every time, every week, every game,” the Belgian added. “Because in the last away games in Europe, you see that they’re a little bit scared to do things, to take risks or to give spaces away.

“But the progress of the team is amazing. The team spirit, I saw it from the first session. They want to learn. They wanted to have feedback, they want to go into it and the kind of football we played. This is the result, they get rewarded, and I’m so happy for them.”

Sports.title: Uefa to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat
Sports.content:
Uefa is to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup.

European teams have been cleared for participation in the upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.

Uefa had threatened the ­boycott after Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal was revealed and ­doubled down after it was ­withdrawn, saying the condition that “such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again” had not been met.

Quick Guide How do I 

Despite exchanging barbs in ­public, Uefa and Fifa are understood to have been having private ­discussions over the terms of ­removing the ­boycott threat for several weeks, with the European governing body finally ­getting the reassurances it required.

When Fifa confirmed its decision to abandon FFE four days after it became public it neglected to pledge that a similar privatisation plan would not be repeated, but it has now done so in private correspondence.

The decision to drop the boycott allows England, who named their squad for the under-20 tournament last week, to travel to Poland in time for the opening game against Canada on 5 September. France and Spain had also listed their travelling party in anticipation that the boycott threat would be lifted. Portugal, Italy and the host nation are the other European countries due to compete.

View image in fullscreen England’s under-20s will travel to the World Cup in Poland. Photograph: Carlos Rodrigues/The FA/Getty Images

Fifa welcomed the end of the boycott , saying: “Fifa is pleased that all qualified teams ‌will be participating in the upcoming Fifa Under-20 Women’s World Cup. Fifa strongly believes that football has the power to unite, even in challenging circumstances, and looks forward to welcoming all teams and players to Poland.”

The boycott is yet to be publicly dropped by Uefa, whose executive committee and federation chiefs meet in Monte Carlo on Thursday. The 55 heads of Uefa’s member associations will convene before the Champions League draw during what is traditionally a significant few days in the European football calendar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Uefa’s position that Infantino must be replaced has not changed and further steps regarding its stance towards the Fifa leadership will also be discussed at the meeting.

Italy’s football federation (FIGC) on Wednesday became the latest to publicly withdraw support for Infantino. “This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC’s position … regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the Fifa president concerning the governance and development of international competitions,” it said.

There will be relief in some quarters that younger players, in particular, will not become embroiled in the volatile battle for football’s future. But the fact that Fifa has been forced to mitigate for its president’s actions is another humiliation for a persistently scandal-hit organisation.

Sports.title: 11-cap England international could make emotional return to boyhood club after West Ham nightmare
Sports.content:
11-cap England international could make emotional return to boyhood club after West Ham nightmare

Southampton are looking into re-signing James Ward-Prowse from West Ham, talkSPORT understands.

The midfielder spent 20 years at St Mary's, having graduated from the club's academy, before leaving the club in 2023 to sign for the Hammers.



3 Ward-Prowse joined West Ham in a £30million deal in 2023 and is in the final year of his contract with the club Credit: Getty

Ward-Prowse joined the Saints at the age of eight, and went on to play 410 senior games for them during his long spell.

Overall, the 31-year-old scored 55 goals and provided 52 assists between 2011 and 2023.

And he could now be offered a route back to his boyhood club, which would bring an end to a tough period at West Ham.



In total, the midfielder has made 75 appearances for West Ham, but he may well be set for an emotional return home.

Homecoming for Ward-Prowse?

Despite a promising first season in east London, Ward-Prowse has gradually slipped down the pecking order at the Hammers.



He spent the 2024/25 campaign on loan at Nottingham Forest, but featured just ten times under Nuno Espirito Santo at the City Ground.

And things went from bad to worse when the Portuguese was appointed Hammers boss in September 2025.



Ward-Prowse was almost immediately frozen out by Nuno, and was forced to train alone before joining Burnley on loan.

With both West Ham and Burnley suffering relegation to the Championship last term, the 11-cap England international has since returned to the London Stadium.

He has featured twice as a substitute this term - in the Irons' opening day 2-2 draw with the Clarets, and in their Carabao Cup first round win over Portsmouth.

3 Ward-Prowse was named Southampton captain 2020 Credit: Getty



However, Ward-Prowse was denied a homecoming against Southampton on Tuesday, as he was left out of West Ham's squad for their Carabao Cup second round victory at St Mary's.

The Hammers' ran out 4-1 winners, with head coach Nuno confirming the midfielder was fit but not selected.

He told the Southern Daily Echo: "We have to make the list, we have to make the list.

"Many of our players stayed at Rush Green [the club's training ground], and it's normal."



And with Ward-Prowse out of contract next summer, it remains to be seen whether he will remain at West Ham beyond transfer deadline day.

Southampton would certainly welcome additions in midfielder, after losing key man Shea Charles to Fulham in a £30million deal.

3 It remains to be seen whether Nuno Espirito Santo will allow Ward-Prowse to join the West Ham exodus Credit: Getty

But West Ham could prove difficult negotiators, who have experienced something of an exodus this summer.



Mateus Fernandes joined rivals Tottenham in a £85m deal, before Crysencio Summerville signed for Saudi outfit Al Hilal for £68m.

The east Londoners were then dealt a fresh blow when academy graduate Freddie Potts completed a £10m move to Belgian side Club Brugge, while left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf continues to be linked with a move to Brentford.

Sports.title: Liverpool face Tottenham as Arsenal, Man City and Man United discover Carabao Cup opponents
Sports.content:
Fixtures for the Carabao Cup third round have been confirmed, with Liverpool drawn against Tottenham in a monster tie.

The Reds are entering the competition at this round due to playing in Europe this season, and they've got a tough clash at Anfield coming their way to start.

2 Spurs booked a round three date at Anfield after a 5-1 thumping of Charlton, in a tie that saw Savinho score on debut Credit: Getty

Spurs easily progressed through in the cup after thrashing Championship side Charlton 5-1 on Wednesday evening, in a game that saw new signing Savinho score and assist on debut.

But they're going to face a fellow Premier League giant as a reward, with Arsenal, Manchester City and Manchester United all finding out their first cup opponents of the campaign too.

The Gunners will be taking on Ipswich Town at Portman Road in the third round following the draw.

Meanwhile, 2025 winners Man City are going to face Norwich and Man United come up against Brighton.

Aston Villa, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Crystal Palace are also playing in Europe this season, so they have freshly joined the competition.

Villa take on Frank Lampard's Coventry, with Sunderland playing Hull, Palace taking on Middlesbrough and the Cherries drawing Lincoln City.

As for the other Premier League sides, Newcastle and Everton progressed on Wednesday night, with the Magpies next facing Millwall and the Toffees facing Wolves.

Chelsea play Luton on Thursday, and should they win, they will take on top-flight rivals Leeds at Stamford Bridge.

Fulham vs Wimbledon is the other Carabao Cup second round fixture still to be played, with the winner facing West Ham.

Newcastle vs Millwall is another of the standout ties.
