Sports.title: Arsenal and Man City could have transfer showdown for £80m-rated Premier League forward
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Man City could have transfer showdown for £80m-rated Premier League forward

Manchester City and Arsenal are showing an interest in Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye, talkSPORT understands.

The Senegal star is unlikely to come cheap though, with the Toffees believed to value him at £80million.

4 Ndiaye scored six goals and provided three assists in 32 league appearances for Everton last term Credit: Getty

Ndiaye has been heavily linked with a departure this summer, and came close to joining Saudi Pro League outfit Al Hilal.

A move ultimately did not materialise, and the 26-year-old has since begun the Premier League campaign with Everton.

But Ndiaye's future has continued to hang in the balance, having turned down a new contract offer to stay in Merseyside earlier this summer.

This would appear to leave him open to a move away, and it could be hard to ignore Man City should their interest progress.

The Citizens aren't the only top side keen on Ndiaye either, with Arsenal also understood to be considering him among their options.

While the Gunners' dream target remains Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez, the player is known to favour a difficult move to Barcelona.

And if the Premier League champions miss out on Alvarez, they could well turn their attention to Ndiaye.

Hot commodity

Ndiaye has impressed since joining from Marseille in 2024, and is under contract until the summer of 2029.

He scored six goals and provided three assists in 32 league appearances for the Toffees last term.

The attacker was also part of Senegal's World Cup squad, scoring once and adding two assists as they reached the last 32.

4 Enzo Maresca and Mikel Arteta could be set to battle it out for Ndiaye's signature Credit: Getty

4 The Senegalese has made 71 appearances overall for the Toffees, scoring 17 goals Credit: Getty

Ndiaye played all 90 minutes of Everton's Premier League opener against Crystal Palace on Saturday.

He played a key role as the Toffees ran out 2-0 winners, assisting Thierno Barry with a jinking run and inch-perfect cross.

Having proven himself to be a real asset in the Premier League, Arsenal and Man City could be set for a transfer tug-of-war over Ndiaye.

Both teams will be keen to strengthen their forward lines before the transfer window slams shut on September 1, not least the Citizens.

Enzo Maresca's side recently bid farewell to Savinho, who finally joined Tottenham in a deal worth up to £85m.

And they look set to lose another attacking player, with Omar Marmoush also on the verge of joining Spurs on a season-long loan switch with an obligation to buy.

4 Savinho's move to Tottenham may have forced Man City to pursue Ndiaye Credit: Getty

As for Arsenal, Mikel Arteta has made bolstering their forward line a real priority this summer.

Christos Tzolis completed a £34m move to the reigning champions earlier in the summer, while the Gunners ultimately missed out in their high-profile pursuit of Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior.

And should they fail to land Argentina star Alvarez, Ndiaye could be exactly the proven Premier League star they target next.

Sports.title: Jack Grealish handed career lifeline by two Premier League clubs as Sunderland approach denied
Sports.content:
Aston Villa and Everton are both interested in signing Jack Grealish on loan, talkSPORT understands.

It was reported on Wednesday that Sunderland had made a bid to sign Grealish, however, City sources have denied any official approach from Sunderland for the player.

3 Grealish joined City in 2021 but faces an uncertain future Credit: Getty

With the England international in the final year of his City contract, he would effectively be saying goodbye to the club should he secure a loan switch this summer.

Grealish has featured twice this season for City, coming on in the second half in the Community Shield against Arsenal as well as in the club's Premier League opener against Bournemouth.

Prior to the season starting, the forward was given the No. 18 shirt at City in a sign he may have a future at the club.

He had previously worn No. 10, but that number now belongs to Rayan Cherki.

New City boss Enzo Maresca has previously suggested that Grealish could play a role at City this season but hasn't ruled out a move for the player either.

"He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best," Maresca said of Grealish after their 2-1 win over the Cherries last weekend.

"Then it is one more week to go and we will see what happens. Not only with Jack but also other players."

Jack Grealish's tricky spell

Grealish spent the 2025/26 campaign on loan with Everton and began brightly, registering four assists in his first three league appearances for the Toffees.

However, his time on Merseyside was brought to an early end when he was forced to undergo surgery on a stress fracture in his foot.

In total, Grealish registered two goals and six assists in 22 appearances for the Toffees.

3 Grealish grew up as a Villa fan and came through the ranks at the club to captain them Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Return to boyhood club?

The other club in contention to sign Grealish on a temporary basis is the team he left to join City for in Villa.

Grealish first joined Villa's academy at the age of six and broke into the first team as an 18-year-old in 2013.

The 30-year-old became a regular fixture in their starting XI from the 2014/15 season, playing a key role in their run to the FA Cup final.

The following campaign was a disaster for Villa as they were relegated from the top flight, finishing bottom of the league.

It took three years of Championship football before the Villans bounced back to the Premier League, but Grealish stuck by them throughout - although he nearly joined Tottenham in 2018.

After starring for Villa in the top flight once again and establishing himself in the England squad, the bigger clubs came calling for Grealish.

3 Grealish became a cult hero when donning an England jersey, especially during Euro 2020 Credit: Getty

Having been linked with moves to Manchester United, Grealish opted to join City in the summer of 2021 for £100million which was then a record transfer for a British player.

Grealish has won a plethora of trophies in his six years at City, including a Premier League, FA Cup and Champions League treble in the 2022/23 season.

However, he often found himself out of the first team, leading to a loan spell at Everton last term.

Grealish has 39 caps for England to his name, scoring four times. He represented the Three Lions at Euro 2020 and 2022 World Cup.

At Villa, Grealish won the club's Player of the Season award on two occasions.

Earlier this summer, talkSPORT host and Villa icon Gabby Agbonlahor tipped the Englishman for a return to his boyhood club, insisting the club's supporters would welcome him back with open arms.

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins to join Al Hilal as deal agreed with Aston Villa to sign replacement instantly
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins to join Al Hilal as deal agreed with Aston Villa to sign replacement instantly

Ollie Watkins is set to formalise a £51million move to Saudi Arabian club Al Hilal, talkSPORT understands.

This comes after Villa agreed a £65m deal with Chelsea over the signing of striker Nicolas Jackson.



4 Watkins is set for a new challenge in the Middle East Credit: Getty

4 But Jackson will immediately replace him Credit: Getty

Villa were reluctant to sell Watkins but the player was pushing for a move, having been left out of the squad for their 4-0 defeat at Brighton last weekend.

And the England international is set to get his way, with Villa and Hilal reaching an agreement in principle for the player in a £51m deal.



The 30-year-old moved to Villa Park from Brentford in 2020 and was part of the side that won the Europa League last season.

Watkins has scored 108 goals in 278 appearances across all competitions for Villa.



The Villans will soon have an instant replacement with Senegal international Jackson set to join, having begun discussions with Chelsea in July.

Unai Emery previously worked with Jackson, who Chelsea value at £65m, during their time at Villarreal.



Tammy Abraham and 17-year-old Brian Madjo represent Jackson's main competition up front at Villa.

Al Hilal's striker search

talkSPORT also understands Al Hilal held talks with Harry Kane over a potential move for the England captain.

However, as previously revealed by talkSPORT, he is expected to stay at Bayern Munich.

The Saudi side are also set to sign Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli in a £49m, plus £7m in add-ons deal.



4 Al Hilal have also held talks with Kane, but he is expected to stay at Bayern Credit: Getty

Former Bournemouth technical director Simon Francis is playing a key role in the pursuit of a new centre-forward.

It comes amid uncertainty surrounding Karim Benzema's future at the club.

The 38-year-old joined Al Hilal from Al Ittihad in February on a deal until the summer of 2027.



talkSPORT understands talks were held between Benzema and the club last month over his future.

He is believed to want a prominent role as opposed to a scenario which would see him only registered for Asian Champions League matches.

It's also understood Al Hilal could offload Darwin Nunez on loan to fellow Saudi Pro League club Diriyah this summer.

4 Watkins will leave Villa after six years of service Credit: Getty



Meanwhile, Francis joined Al Hilal in a senior recruiting role at the start of July after leaving the Cherries.

Simone Inzaghi's side have already signed Crysencio Summerville from West Ham this summer.

The Netherlands winger completed a £68million move to the club last month.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold told surprise Premier League club he’d be brilliant on loan at
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold would be the perfect fit for Newcastle if they could get him on loan.

That’s the view of European football expert Andy Brassell, who analysed what the defender’s role at Real Madrid could be this season.



4 Alexnader-Arnold joined Real Madrid from Liverpool last summer Credit: Getty

Alexander-Arnold flattered to deceive in his first season at Madrid, often playing second fiddle to veteran Dani Carvajal.

Carvajal left this summer and many assumed that would give the 27-year-old an increased role.

Jose Mourinho was appointed manager and one of his first signings was Dutch right-back Denzel Dumfries from Inter Milan.



Dumfries started Madrid’s first game of the season against Espanyol, with Alexander-Arnold playing a late cameo.

Alexander-Arnold’s role at Real Madrid

Brassell told talKSPORT: “I love Trent Alexander-Arnold, but what makes him so difficult to match with the club is not anything to do with his ability, because ability-wise he's impeccable.



“It's that he's a player who people look at and think, because he's so talented in an attacking sense and he's such a good passer, people feel that he's probably a wing-back. But he's not.

“He's most effective in a back four. I know people have criticised his defending over the years, but because he's not a typical overlapping full-back and he's not about beating men.



“He's about being able to play the best pass you've ever seen really early, that makes him a better right-back in a back-four than a wing-back.

“With a wing-back, you want someone who's going to rampage on the outside.

“There's definitely a feeling when they went out and made signings and they signed a guy in Denzel Dumfries who is someone who's very comfortable, a right-back who's very comfortable with a lot of the game going through him.

4 Dumfries started against Espanyol last weekend Credit: Getty



“He's a very different right-back to Trent Alexander-Arnold, because he's a guy who will go outside and will beat a man.

“He's not a guy who's going to ping loads of crosses in the box. It makes you think, if he's one of Mourinho's first signings, is that indicative of what Mourinho wants from a full-back?

“If that's the case, well, Trent Alexander-Arnold is either going to change position, as has been suggested, maybe play in midfield, or he's not going to play a lot.”

Alexander-Arnold perfect for Newcastle?

The right-back will be on huge wages at Madrid, meaning a move, even on loan, would be prohibitive for most clubs.

This would likely mean a Premier League team are the most likely candidates.



If this was not a return to Liverpool, then Brassell picked out Newcastle as an ideal fit.

“Other than that, I think it is really difficult, because it would be a Prem team.

4 Alexander-Arnold won the Premier League twice with Liverpool Credit: AFP

“He'd be brilliant for Newcastle, who, before they went out and bought Amir Dedic, were definitely looking for a right-back.



“I know they spent a lot of money on Dedic and they will have limited means. If you could loan Alexander-Arnold to Newcastle for a year, he would be brilliant there, especially with the pace they've got.

“Imagine the switches of play that he could engineer. Maybe that's not an appealing move to him, to go to a rebuilding team in the Premier League.

“The reality is because of financial reasons, the Premier League is probably the most obvious place for him to go.

“If it's not Liverpool, there's a very limited pool.

“He's such a brilliant player, who is massively underappreciated, and kind of treated as a problem, rather than a solution to a problem.



Alexander-Arnold reunited with Salah?

Another option would be the Turkish Super Lig, who are capable of paying the sort of wages that Alexander-Arnold would be on.

His former teammate Mohamed Salah just so happens to be at Trabzonspor.

Brassell added: “I look at Trent and I think he's a little bit like the Glenn Hoddle of his time, in that no one with half a brain is arguing that he's not a great player, but to fit him in a team is actually quite difficult, to optimise his qualities.

“I don't think you get a better fit anywhere than you get with Alexander-Arnold and Salah together at Liverpool.



4 Salah moved to Turkey after leaving Liverpool this summer Credit: Getty

“That's immediately put in my head, what if Trabzonspor were going to go and get him?

“I know that seems like an obvious link, but you're talking about a league that's got a lot of money.

“If he's going to go somewhere from Real Madrid, unless he's taken a massive wage cut, it's not elsewhere in Spain, it's not to Italy, where does he end up? Maybe the Super Lig at some point. I would absolutely love to see him reunited with Mo Salah.



“Mo Salah would go and pick him up in his car from Madrid, if he thought he could get him, and drive him back to Istanbul, because they were so good together.

“I think it's something that's not really talked about that much.

“When Alexander-Arnold went, it exposed a lot of the other weaknesses in Salah's game. He wasn't able to do what he normally did.

“I don't think he took Trent Alexander-Arnold for granted, but maybe other people took what Trent Alexander-Arnold did for Salah for granted.

“If you put the two of them together, it makes them Turkish champions straight away. There's no partnership like it.



“Whether they've got enough left in the piggy bank after Salah to make that happen, who knows?”

Sports.title: Aston Villa to smash transfer record as they close in on Nicolas Jackson signing
Sports.content:
Aston Villa to smash transfer record as they close in on Nicolas Jackson signing

Aston Villa are closing in on the signing of Nicolas Jackson in a £65million deal, talkSPORT understands.

The deal would allow Ollie Watkins to complete his move to Al Hilal.

2 Jackson is set to swap west London for Birmingham this summer if Villa get their way Credit: Getty



Jackson, is set to become Villa's record arrival with their current record signing being Johan Manzambi, who joined from Freiburg earlier this summer for just north of £50m.

This will be welcome news for Villa, who suffered a major setback with Crystal Palace hijacking their move to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez.

Villa's failed pursuit of the Ecuador international comes after they had two offers rejected by Southampton for Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

But talkSPORT understands Villa are back in talks with Saints for the player with the Championship club open to a sale if Villa are prepared to do a deal worth £25-£30m.



Harwood-Bellis is believed to want to join Villa, who will play Champions League football this season.

Villa are also considering a move for Jean-Clair Todibo, who is currently on strike as he desperately seeks a move away from West Ham.



Who has left Aston Villa this summer?

Villa have been pilloried this summer, with Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne all sold.

And the high-profile exits may not be done there, with Al Hilal still confident they can land Watkins before the window shuts.



Meanwhile, Emi Martinez is keen on a move to Chelsea following the arrival of Zion Suzuki from Parma.

The Saudi outfit have had numerous offers for Watkins rejected but personal terms are already in place if the two clubs can agree a fee.

2 Watkins has scored 108 goals in 278 appearances for Villa Credit: Getty

Watkins was a notable absentee from Villa's squad that was thrashed 4-0 by Brighton on Sunday.



What has Unai Emery said about Ollie Watkins' future?

Curiously, Villa boss Unai Emery refused to confirm whether Watkins requested to be left out of the team amid Al-Hilal's ongoing pursuit.

"This question is for him," Emery said.

"I can answer only with my silence."

Emery added: "I think you call his agent and he can respond. He can only explain his answer, I can't."

Watkins, who did not train with Villa in the lead-up to the Brighton defeat, later apologised to his teammates on Monday.

Sports.title: Chelsea send email urging fans to bin sectarian chant sung during Fulham clash
Sports.content:
Chelsea have warned fans they could face an 'indefinite suspension' should they be found guilty of singing a sectarian chant.

In an email sent to supporters, the Blues hailed their 'passion and backing' during the 3-2 win over Fulham at Craven Cottage on Monday.



2 Chelsea fans were in fine voice on Stamford Bridge, although they have been reminded not to sing certain chants Credit: Getty

However, the club confirmed it received reports a 'small portion' of the travelling fans engaged in sectarian chanting.

Chelsea issue stern warning over sectarian chants

"We would like to strongly remind all supporters that the club does not condone any chants which discriminate against a protected characteristic," Chelsea wrote.

"Any supporter found guilty of this will face the strongest possible action, which could include indefinite suspension from attending all Chelsea matches and ejection from the stadium.



"Following previous club fines and charges for chants of this nature, and to ensure that we create a welcoming matchday experience for all, we ask supporters to take collective responsibility and remain vigilant in helping us to tackle discriminatory chanting."

Chelsea were fined over £8,000 in January 2025 for singing an anti-IRA chant during a 5-1 win over Shamrock Rovers in the Conference League.



How Chelsea's Premier League opener against Fulham unfolded

The Blues began Monday's contest against Fulham in brilliant fashion, with Joao Pedro putting the visitors in front within the opening minute.

However, Chelsea's lead lasted just over 20 minutes as Joshua King equalised.



It was a moment Blues goalkeeper Robert Sanchez would rather forget as he failed to make what appeared to be a simple save and instead dived too late.

Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea earlier this summer for a British record £117million, restored the visitors' lead just before half time before Cole Palmer doubled the advantage in the 49th minute.

Gonzalo Garcia pulled one back for the hosts five minutes later, but the Blues held on for all three points.

2 The Xabi Alonso era at Chelsea has got off to a brilliant start Credit: Getty



Speaking after the contest, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso believed the performance was the perfect platform to build from.

What did Xabi Alonso say about Chelsea's win over Fulham?

"It feels very good for sure, and you know how tough it is to win any Premier League game, any Premier League away game, but we were prepared for an intense game," Alonso said.

"I think it's been a very professional, solid performance, with maturity, matching different momentum during the game.

"We got the lead quite early, we had chances to score the second goal a few times, and after the equalise we went through ten minutes when we had not chosen the right [way] to press and the movement, but we have corrected well this, and in the second half we have felt comfortable without the ball controlling the game.



"I think it's a performance to build for the future, improve things for sure, but it's a good first day."

Alonso will look to make it two wins from two on Thursday when Chelsea host Luton Town in the second round of the Carabao Cup, with kick-off scheduled for 7:30pm.

Sports.title: Ex-Arsenal villain Matteo Guendouzi sparks shocking Champions League brawl - with rival staff member trying to ATTACK star - after he delivered x-rated gesture to Lyon fans before Fenerbahce win
Sports.content:
Ex-Arsenal villain Matteo Guendouzi sparks shocking Champions League brawl - with rival staff member trying to ATTACK star - after he delivered x-rated gesture to Lyon fans before Fenerbahce win

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Arsenal midfielder Matteo Guendouzi appeared to be attacked by a goalkeeping coach after he sparked a wild brawl in shocking scenes at the end of the Champions League play-off between Lyon and Fenerbahce.

Guendouzi goaded Lyon supporters as he left the field after the Turkish side had booked their spot in the league phase with a 2-1 victory at the Groupama Stadium.

The 27-year-old's antics were met with a furious response from a man dressed in a Lyon tracksuit, later identified by French newspaper L'Equipe as the club's goalkeeping coach Antonio Ferreira.

Chaotic footage taken from the stands shows Ferreira emerging from the tunnel and seemingly aiming a flying kick at Guendouzi as he walked off.

Players and staff from both sides then rushed towards the tunnel before a violent melee broke out, with punches thrown in the direction of Ferreira as he was pinned against a wall. Security staff could also be seen holding back players and coaches.

The incident came at the end of a tempestuous contest, with Guendouzi at the centre of the controversy.

🚨🚨 The aftermath of the Lyon vs Fenerbahçe match. 😳👊 pic.twitter.com/maRawLYIOu — EuroFoot (@eurofootcom) August 26, 2026

Lyon's goalkeeping coach appeared to attack Matteo Guendouzi in a fiery post-match brawl

Guendouzi had seemingly taunted Lyon players and supporters as he walked towards the tunnel

Shocking footage also showed Antonio Ferreira pinned against a wall as punches were thrown

Players and coaches from both teams were involved in the melee in the tunnel area

The former Gunners villain spent two seasons at Lyon's arch-rivals Marseille, and was seen giving home fans the finger before kick-off and during the game in response to a chorus of boos and jeers aimed in his direction.

Tempers later flared on the pitch with reports claiming Guendouzi shouted 'we're f****ng you' towards his opponents when his team went 2-0 up.

Lyon players then reacted angrily at full-time and shoved the Frenchman before his Fenerbahce team-mates, including Ederson and Romelu Lukaku, rushed to his defence.

Guendouzi also reportedly taunted Lyon fans again with a reference to Marseille, where he made 103 appearances, as he walked off the pitch.

He seemingly ignored his team-mates' attempts to calm him down as he continued his celebrations with his actions causing a post-match brawl that could land both clubs in hot water with UEFA.

Lyon's Corentin Tolisso hit out at Guendouzi after the fiery encounter. 'You have to stay humble in victory, go celebrate that with your team in the locker room,' he said. 'Well done, congratulations to them, but there's no real need to do that.'

It is far from the first time Guendouzi has been involved in controversy. He joined Arsenal in 2018 but left the club after being banished from the squad by Mikel Arteta in the summer of 2020 following an infamous spat with Brighton's Neal Maupay.

Guendouzi – who had reportedly taunted Brighton players about their salary and ability in the clash at the Amex Stadium during 'project restart' – was caught by TV cameras grabbing Maupay by the throat at the end of the game.

Former Marseille star Guendouzi was seen repeatedly given the middle finger to home fans

Tempers flared during a dramatic second leg, which Fenerbahce won to progress to the league phase

The midfielder never played for the Gunners again and was shipped out to Hertha Berlin before he joined Marseille.

Guendouzi had been involved in trouble before he moved to Arsenal. During his time at Lorient, he was excluded from the first team for more than three months because of a dressing-room clash with team-mates.

Fenerbahce will be in the draw for the league phase of the Champions League on Thursday following the victory, with Lyon dropping into the Europa League after a 3-2 aggregate defeat.

The Turkish side will be in pot three for the draw, which begins at 5pm UK time.

Sports.title: Bodycam footage shows humiliating moment 49ers owner Jed York is arrested in trailer park after trying to meet up with $140 prostitute
Sports.content:
The Daily Mail can reveal the humiliating bodycam footage that shows 49ers owner and CEO Jed York being arrested after showing up at an Ohio trailer park to allegedly pay a prostitute $140 for sex.

York, who is worth $500 million and also co-owns Premier League club Leeds United and Scottish giants Rangers, was arrested in East Palestine on suspicion of engaging in prostitution at 9.35am on August 23. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.

Court documents obtained by The Daily Mail reveal York, 46, 'arranged to have sexual activity with the female in exchange for $140.' He responded to an undercover ad placed on a known prostitution website by law enforcement.

When York arrived at the arranged location, the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in East Palestine, York was greeted by a law enforcement sting operation.

Footage of that moment has now been obtained by The Daily Mail and shows the moment York - still wearing his wedding ring - is pulled from his car and placed in handcuffs by cops.

In the excruciating footage, the NFL owner is asked what he is doing at the trailer park, to which he replies: 'Just driving.' When quizzed over whether he is meeting anyone, he simply replies: 'No'.

San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York is confronted by police officers in a prostitution sting

The NFL owner, who is said to be worth $500m, quickly put his hands above his head

York, 46, was arrested Sunday in East Palestine, Ohio, and booked into Columbiana County Jail

York is wearing a New York Yankees shirt, basketball shorts and tennis shoes in the footage, released to the Daily Mail by the East Palestine Police Department.

As the footage continues, York is placed in handcuffs by officers and asked if he is from the local area, to which he responds: 'Yeah'.

The officer says to him, 'so you're just driving around East Palestine?', and York again gives a simple one-word affirmative.

York is taken to the back seat of the police vehicle, where he is placed inside and the door is shut. The officers then have a conversation next to a separate vehicle, of which the audio has been redacted from the released footage.

As the video footage continues, one of the officers searches York's rental vehicle and finds $160 in cash - which was seized and later given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement.

The arresting officers do not appear to be aware of the high-profile role York holds, with one heard telling his colleague: 'He's a real estate guy, he's got all the money.'

After York is taken away by one cop in a black patrol car, the initial arresting officer places a phone call with a colleague and goes back to York's car, where he finds two phones - one of which features an image of his two sons as the background.

The absent officer sends a text message to York's burner phone, and the pair then discuss some of the content of York's messages, allegedly sent to who he believed was a prostitute he was meeting.

'Yeah, he said he was from Chicago, real estate,' the officer says.

York told the police officers he was 'just driving' when he was arrested near a trailer park

Cops retrieved two phones from his rental car, one of which carrying a photo of his two sons

York was taken into custody when an agent with the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force discovered York had 'in his possession his cellular device which was used to arrange a criminal act', court documents show.

York, who was born 20 miles away from East Palestine in Youngstown, Ohio, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He was also charged with possessing criminal tools.

York was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.

Records also show that York had a cellphone returned to him, and that he also completed an online course.

It comes after York filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, back in May and cited irreconcilable differences.

The San Francisco Chronicle has reported the couple are still waiting for a court date for their dissolution of marriage case to be heard.

The couple, who got married in 2011, have two sons, Jaxon and Brixton. They have agreed to legal and physical joint custody.

The NFL said in a statement: 'We are aware of the matter, which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.'

York - above with wife Danielle - allegedly attempted to pay a woman $140 for sex

Cops lured York to the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community before arresting him on Sunday

The 49ers said in a statement: 'As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time.'

The Daily Mail has reached out to East Palestine Police and the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, as well as York's attorney for comment.

York is the son of Denise DeBartolo York and John York. They took control of the 49ers when DeBartolo's brother, Eddie, was convicted in a gambling fraud scandal.

Eddie, who owned the 49ers during their 1980s-1990s dynasty, pleaded guilty in 1998 to failing to report a felony when he paid $400,000 to former Louisiana Governor Edwin Edwards in exchange for a riverboat gambling license.

DeBartolo, whose 49ers won five Super Bowls under his leadership, stepped down as owner in 1997 after two Louisiana newspapers reported he would be indicted for gambling fraud.

York has been married to Belluomini since 2011 and they have two sons together

The 49ers play their play their first game against the LA Rams in Melbourne on September 19

He avoided prison, was fined $1 million and was suspended for a year by the NFL but the episode effectively ended his NFL career. President Donald Trump pardoned him in February 2020.

Jed began working for his father in the early 2000s and was eventually named the franchise's CEO in 2008. He then became the principal owner in 2024 after acquiring enough of his mother's stake.

During his tenure, the Niners have experienced great success, having won five NFC West titles, advanced to seven NFC Championship Games and three Super Bowls, although the team has not won the NFL's biggest prize since 1994.

York also oversaw the building of Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California. The team moved from San Francisco to the new stadium in 2014. The stadium has hosted two Super Bowls, a World Cup and a College Football Playoff title game.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho's perfect Bernabeu return: Kylian Mbappe scores hat-trick as Real Madrid thump Real Sociedad - and jubilant Spanish media claim Jude Bellingham is coach's 'star signing' after 'stellar' performance
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho's perfect Bernabeu return: Kylian Mbappe scores hat-trick as Real Madrid thump Real Sociedad - and jubilant Spanish media claim Jude Bellingham is coach's 'star signing' after 'stellar' performance

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jose Mourinho's first game back at the Santiago Bernabeu as Real Madrid manager got off to a winning start after a thumping 4-1 victory over Real Sociedad.

Kylian Mbappe scored a hat-trick as the Spanish giants won their first home match of the LaLiga season.

While Real's star striker collected the match ball, it was he and Jude Bellingham who picked up the accolades for their performances.

Spanish outlet Marca gave Mbappe a 10/10 for his display, while Bellingham received a nine.

While Mbappe was labelled 'devastating', Marca's praise for Bellingham was noteworthy too who they called 'Mourinho's star signing'.

Describing his first-half showing as an 8/10, Marca writes: 'Giving the impression of being in peak physical condition and without losing the spark he rediscovered at the World Cup.

Jude Bellingham (left) shone for Real Madrid as Jose Mourinho's first game back at the Santiago Bernabeu as manager ended in a resounding 4-1 LaLiga win over Real Sociedad

Kylian Mbappe took the match ball home after scoring a hat-trick in Wednesday's victory

Mourinho has plenty to smile about after recording his second-straight win since taking over

'Intense, aggressive, appearing everywhere and playing with clarity and precision. He was very dangerous on the edge of the box and created good chances for Mbappe and Vini [Vinicius Jr].

'He appealed for a clear free-kick on the edge of the area, which Busquets Ferrer denied. He drew a yellow card from Yangel Herrera.'

The Madrid-based outlet then purrs over the 23-year-old's second-half showing which increases to 9/10, writing: 'Stellar. The Bernabeu's ovation when he was substituted was proof of a fantastic match full of commitment, effort, and moments of quality.

'An exquisite one-two with Mbappe on the edge of the box left the Frenchman alone for the 2-1. A truly world-class piece of skill. But there was more. His great individual effort and fighting spirit led to the assist he provided for Vinicius's third goal.

'Bellingham is Mourinho's star signing.'

High praise indeed.

Mbappe put Madrid ahead in the 40th minute before Luka Sucic levelled four minutes later but the France forward restored the hosts' lead on the hour and Vinicius Jr added a third in the 68th before Mbappe completed his treble 10 minutes from time.

It was also a winning return to the Santiago Bernabeu for Mourinho, more than 13 years after his previous home match in charge of the club, as Real recovered from a disjointed first half with a ruthless display after the break.

Marca described Bellingham's display as 'stellar' and labelled him Mourinho's 'star signing'

Madrid were jeered before half-time after a sluggish opening in which they looked short of rhythm, careless in possession and vulnerable on the counter-attack.

'There's always a sense of justice in the boos and the applause, and the odd boo now and then doesn't do anyone any harm - it helps you grow,' Mourinho told a press conference.

'We all know the Santiago Bernabeu and just how demanding the fans are there, and I'm very pleased with how my players responded under pressure and put in a great second half, in which we could even have scored more goals.'

Sociedad carried the sharper threat early on and almost went ahead in the 10th minute when Take Kubo intercepted a loose pass near the edge of the box and slipped in Mikel Oyarzabal, whose close-range effort was kept out by Thibaut Courtois.

The visitors went close again in the 34th minute, Sergio Gomez flashing a fine volley just wide of the far post, as the Bernabeu crowd began to voice its frustration.

Mbappe briefly changed the mood five minutes before half-time with a flash of class. Federico Valverde collected the ball just beyond midfield and split the defense with a superb pass, allowing Mbappe to surge into the box, cut left and lash a shot into the top corner.

But Real's defensive uncertainty returned four minutes later. Ibrahima Konate, Dean Huijsen and Alvaro Carreras were all caught out after Job Ochieng latched on to a long ball, his deflected effort falling to Luka Sucic on the right, who had time to steady himself and drill a low shot past Courtois.

Mbappe watches on as his shot heads towards the net during Real's emphatic LaLiga victory

Mourinho sent on Marc Cucurella at half-time and Madrid emerged transformed, with Vinicius Jr and Mbappe stretching the visitors with direct running and greater intensity.

The hosts regained the lead on the hour when Mbappe and Bellingham exchanged a sharp one-two, leaving the France forward free inside the box to beat Alex Remiro with a low finish.

Eight minutes later, Bellingham's pressing won the ball back near the byline and his low cross gave Vinicius the simplest of tap-ins from close range.

Mbappe completed the win in the 80th minute after Vinicius slipped a clever pass behind the defense, the forward lifting a composed chip over Remiro to seal his hat-trick.

Speaking post-match about his forward, Mourinho was effusive in his praise, saying: 'There's something I don't like doing, but sometimes I have to do: I don't like to talk about individuals, but what Kylian did …it was insane,' he told Real Madrid TV.

'Mbappe has a knack for scoring, for creating chances… when the team is under pressure, he's able to drop deep and link up with Vini and Jude, gaining ground and creating danger.'

Mourinho's lavish praise of Mbappe continued during his post-match press conference, adding: 'This bloke is incredible. He's incredible. I'm really glad he made history at the World Cup because only one player is truly for the ages, the one with the most World Cup goals. I can see he's absolutely raring to make history with Real Madrid. I've seen a team where, even though Kylian is Kylian and has done what he's done.

'Mbappe arrived two days before his holidays were expected to finish, and those two extra days in pre-season can make a positive difference.'

Sports.title: Alan Shearer confirms he is scaling back Match of the Day appearances and reveals why he will feature just ONCE a month on iconic show - as he wades into Ollie Watkins' Villa row
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer will limit his appearances on Match of the Day to once a month - so he can spend more time watching his beloved Newcastle.

Shearer has provided punditry on the BBC's flagship football programme for 20 years since retiring as the Premier League’s all-time top goalscorer in 2006, but revealed before the start of the new Premier League season that he would be taking a step back from the show.

The former Newcastle striker featured on the programme last weekend, reviewing the Premier League openers alongside Manchester United and England legend Wayne Rooney.

However, viewers were left wondering when he would next appear on the weekly highlight show.

Speaking to Daily Mail Sport, Shearer, an ambassador for Betfair, clarified that he would pop up monthly while continuing to lead the Beeb's commentary on their live FA Cup matches.

Alan Shearer has revealed why he is stepping back from Match of the Duty punditry duties

The Newcastle legend will feature on the iconic football show just once per month

‘I said to them a while back that I would like some of my weekends back on a Saturday, Shearer told Daily Mail Sport. 'It’ll be about one a month.

'I’ll be going to more Newcastle games. I love doing the co-comms. When the FA Cup starts in January, there’s loads of co-comms.’

The Beeb have expanded their punditry team for the new season with Toby Alderweireld, Robbie Keane, Ashley Young and Thomas Frank joining their football coverage.

Shearer, meanwhile, took a dim view of the emerging trend of Premier League players striking to force moves away from their club.

Alexander Isak and Yohane Wissa both downed tools - refusing to train and play - to force moves to Liverpool and Newcastle respectively last summer, while there have been suggestions that Ollie Watkins employed a similar tactic to push through his imminent switch from Aston Villa to Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia.

Tolu Arokodare even stopped a Wolves training session to get his move to Ajax.

'It’s not a good look when you have supporters paying their hard-earned money to watch you and adore you and you get a great salary,' Shearer said.

'I’m not saying Ollie has done that because we don’t have the full story but it’s not right that you refuse to play for your club when they’re paying your wages. It’s a part of football that I don’t like.

'You always have the right to leave any football club, but there’s a way to do it. I left Blackburn a year after we won the Premier League because I wanted to try a different challenge and ended up back at Newcastle.

'I understand it, I get it, nobody can tell you that you can’t do that, you’re well within your right. But there’s a way to do it.'

Isak left Newcastle for Liverpool last summer for a British record £125m but has struggled to settle at Anfield, missing 24 games last term with a broken leg.

When he has played, though, Shearer feels that the Swedish international has struggled because Liverpool do not play to his strengths.

‘I look at when he was brilliant at Newcastle, and how you got the best out of him was early balls in behind or in from behind.

‘I don’t see Liverpool doing that. I guess they will have to change a little bit.

‘It certainly hasn’t worked with Wirtz and him, they’ve paid a fortune for both players.

‘I look at Alex and when he was brilliant at Newcastle, it was them playing early ball from midfielders in behind and wingers out wide early. I don’t see that at Liverpool as yet. It’s a bit of both.

‘He had a serious injury last season but those two are going to have to do miles better if Liverpool are going to get into the top four.’

It has been a brutal summer for Shearer's beloved Newcastle. The North East club lost manager Eddie Howe, who resigned amid significant summer sales with Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali all exiting.

Despite having the richest owners in the world, Newcastle have been forced to become a selling club due to the Premier League and UEFA's financial regulations.

Shearer accepts that it will be a difficult season at St James' Park and does not expect European football but is excited by the appointment of Matthias Jaissle, a charismatic character.

Shearer says he wants to spend more time watching his beloved boyhood club

He took a dim view of players striking to get a transfer, amid speculation over Ollie Watkins

The 56-year-old, who scored 206 goals for Newcastle in ten seasons, bemoaned the rules but conceded refreshing the playing squad is not a bad thing after a difficult campaign last term.

'Plenty of optimism at Newcastle after a long summer. It needed a reset. We mustn’t forget all those players Newcastle sold, wanted to go, didn’t want to be there and didn’t have great seasons last season because Newcastle finished 12th.

'It had to be a reset and it’s going to take a lot of patience at times, albeit hoping for one or two in before the end of the transfer window, then plenty to be optimistic about after the weekend.

'Look at Aston Villa and what they’ve had to do, selling their best players. Chelsea and Man City wouldn’t be where they are if those rules are in place now.

'You get to a point and you can challenge, finish in and around the top five for two or three years but then you see what you have to do to comply with those rules.

'Newcastle have had to do the same because of the laws. I don’t like those but it is what it is, you have to somehow get by and Newcastle have done that. It is a reset. New young manager, new ideas and hopefully plenty to be optimistic about.

'I don’t expect us to get into European football this year. If we do, great, it’ll be a great bonus but I don’t expect that.

'We need another midfielder before the end of the window without a doubt, maybe another player in a forward position. It is a transitional year and we have to accept what is thrown at us because selling your best players and losing your manager is not always easy.

Shearer believes there are reasons to be optimistic for Newcastle fans this season

'If it was easy, everyone would do it and bring in younger players. They’re going to need time to get used to it and improve - they will get better with experience.

'The Newcastle fanbase will understand that and accept what kind of season it is going to be.'

Newcastle swiftly responded to Shearer’s wish for a midfielder, landing Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City for £52million.

Gonzalez spent a season and a half at City after signing from Porto, making 36 Premier League appearances for the club.

The 24-year-old fits Newcastle’s transfer strategy of acquiring young players with a high ceiling and Shearer believes that Gonzalez’s time under Pep Guardiola will add an extra edge to Newcastle.

‘It’s really good business with his experience, being at Manchester City for that amount of time, playing under Pep in that winning culture will do Newcastle the world of good.’

Alan Shearer was speaking on Wembley Way at the launch of Betfair’s Walk of Shame, which immortalises football’s most spectacularly inaccurate predictions and takes. Everyone’s got an opinion, back yours at Betfair.

Sports.title: Savio steals the show on dream Spurs debut: £85m star delivers perfect response to critics after move from Man City as Tottenham thrash Charlton to reach Carabao Cup third round
Sports.content:
Nineteen minutes was all the time required by Savio to deliver the perfect response to anyone who considers £85million too much to pay for an attacking player who neither scores nor creates enough goals. The Brazilian, signed from Manchester City on Monday, came off the bench to mark his debut with a goal and an assist against the second string of second tier Charlton, who were already flagging when he appeared. Savio claimed Tottenham's fourth goal, a delightful low finish on the end of a twinkle-toed dribble and was denied a second goal when another solo effort clipped Ben Davies and went in for the fifth. It went down as a Davies goal, but Roberto De Zerbi hardly cared as his new Spurs flickered into life. After a feeble opening-day demise at Brentford, this was a victory he needed and there were things for him to savour beyond a flying start for the new signing. There were flashes of teenage exuberance from Mikey Moore on the right wing, a strong full debut from Mateus Fernandes in midfield and a first goal of the season from Dominic Solanke. And a first Spurs goal for Kevin Danso, who came off the bench to score with his first touch, a header from a free kick as he collided with a defender and looked briefly as if he might have to come straight off again, before soldiering on with his wounds taped up. Savio scored on his debut for Tottenham following his £85million move from Manchester City The Brazilian came off the bench and made an immediate impact with a goal and an assist De Zerbi's team move into the last 32 of the Carabao Cup and that will soothe the nerves before they return to N17 to face Newcastle on Saturday. Spurs were not always fluent. They encountered familiar problems trying to break down the massed ranks of determined opponents for the first half hour, and they were vulnerable at times at the back, and Lloyd Jones scored late for the visitors. But De Zerbi can call it progress. The Spurs boss claimed the Carabao Cup was no less important than the Premier League on the eve of the game and stressed the importance of establishing a winning habit. Winning matches, not a match but two, three, four matches. This aim was reflected in the club's summer recruitment drive, not only spending big but on players from clubs with cultures of success. Savio from City with Omar Marmoush expected to follow. Andy Robertson from Liverpool. Sandro Tonali from Newcastle, although the £100m-man was not involved against Charlton. Instead, he and Marcos Senesi were put through an intense physical training session on Tuesday to improve their fitness. 'Saturday he will play in the first XI without problems,' said De Zerbi of Tonali. With no European campaign, Spurs would welcome a run in this competition to keep those on the fringes of the squad active. Charlton started the season with three straight wins, but boss Nathan Jones made his priorities clear with 10 changes from the team which beat West Ham in the Championship, four days earlier. Billy Koumetio was the only survivor, and he and his central defensive partner Collins Sichenje were both off injured within 15 minutes. Sichenje hurt a knee in an innocuous clash with Mathys Tel. He tried to continue but soon went down again and left the scene on a stretcher. Koumetio limped off at the same time. 'Absolutely disastrous for us,' said boss Jones. 'The romance is very nice, but this was a game we didn't need.' When the contest settled again, it was the visitors who threatened. Lucas Bergvall was booked for cutting down Rob Apter on a dangerous break. Toni Kinsky made a flying save from Greg Docherty and Nathan Asiimwe headed a chance wide. Six thousand in the away end were encouraged but Spurs took control once they found their rhythm towards the end of the first half. Charlton keeper Tiernan Brooks, making his debut after signing from Gateshead, saved from low to his left from Archie Gray and into his midriff from Fernandes, and his back four protected him with a series of crucial blocks and tackles as pressure mounted. Moore, who scored twice in a 3-0 pre-season win against Hoffenheim, made the breakthrough in the 41st minute. Dancing into the penalty box from the right, the 19-year-old winger capitalised on a slip by Millenic Alli and unleashed a left footer which beat Brooks with the help of a slight deflection. It was his second Spurs goal and his first since January 2025 when he lit up a Europa League tie against Elfsborg and prompted James Maddison to compare him to Neymar. Spurs relaxed and confidence washed through them. Four minutes later, Solanke slammed into the second, on the volley as a loose ball bounced his way in the penalty area. De Zerbi rolled through some changes to good effect. First Danso. Then Savio to add the flourish. De Zerbi's Savio challenge Roberto De Zerbi has challenged £85million signing Savio to score 12 goals this season after an electric start to his Tottenham career. Savio scored 11 minutes into his 19-minute cameo before adding an assist three minutes later during Spurs' 5-1 Carabao Cup second-round win over Charlton. The 22-year-old arrived from Manchester City this week after scoring seven in two years. Spurs boss De Zerbi reckons he has the making of a top winger but must add goals to his game. 'A perfect day for him,' said De Zerbi. 'His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. 'His qualities, he is one of the best wingers but the best wingers score many goals. 'I spoke with him two days ago, and we set the goal of 10-12 goals, we need 10-12 goals from the wingers. 'Last season we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough to compete for more than that position.' By Bobby Manzi at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium

Sports.title: Liverpool to face Spurs in crunch all-Premier League clash as Man United host Brighton and Man City begin defence at home to Norwich: CARABAO CUP THIRD-ROUND DRAW
Sports.content:
Liverpool to face Spurs in crunch all-Premier League clash as Man United host Brighton and Man City begin defence at home to Norwich: CARABAO CUP THIRD-ROUND DRAW

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool will face Tottenham Hotspur in a crunch all-Premier League tie in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

The encounter at Anfield is the pick of the games in the draw held on Wednesday evening.

Manchester United host Brighton, which could see Carlos Baleba take on his old side after he sealed a £70million move to Old Trafford this week.

Manchester City will begin their defence of the Carabao Cup at home to Championship outfit Norwich and Arsenal, beaten by Pep Guardiola's side in the final in March, go to Ipswich.

Chelsea will take on Leeds, should the Blues get past Luton at Stamford Bridge on Thursday, while Aston Villa make the short trip to Frank Lampard's Coventry.

Conference League winners Crystal Palace will start their pursuit of winning silverware for three seasons in a row at home to Middlesbrough, while Newcastle's reward for beating West Brom is a visit to Millwall.

Liverpool host Tottenham in the pick of the Carabao Cup third-round ties after the draw was conducted on Wednesday

CARABAO CUP THIRD-ROUND DRAW Crystal Palace v Middlesbrough Manchester United v Brighton Manchester City v Norwich Sunderland v Hull Ipswich v Arsenal Coventry v Aston Villa Bournemouth v Lincoln Liverpool v Tottenham Chelsea or Luton v Leeds Millwall v Newcastle Fleetwood v Sheffield United Everton v Wolves Leyton Orient v Bradford Reading v Brentford Peterborough v Barnsley West Ham v Fulham or AFC Wimbledon

Bournemouth welcome Lincoln to the Vitality Stadium, Everton host Wolves and Sunderland play Hull in another all-Premier League tie, while Fulham will travel to West Ham if they overcome AFC Wimbledon on Thursday.

Elsewhere, Brentford go to Reading, while League Two Fleetwood, the lowest-ranked side in round three, entertain Sheffield United.

The eight Premier League sides in the Champions League and Europa League this season could not face each other because of a clash with the opening fixtures in the two competitions.

A pre-draw was held ahead of Everton's victory at Preston to determine whether they would play home or away in the third round.

Brighton are in the Conference League play-offs but were excluded from the pre-draw as the competition's league phase does not begin until October.

Matches will be held in the weeks commencing September 7 and 14 to accommodate the schedule for the Champions League and Europa League.

Sports.title: Harvey Barnes rides to the rescue for Newcastle: New boss Matthias Jaissle's substitutions once again prove decisive... but the challenge for £50m new man Nico Gonzalez is clear
Sports.content:
There was an argument to say this was Newcastle's biggest game of the week.

Not because of what it meant in the isolation of these seven days. Premier League matches against Liverpool and Tottenham are far more significant.

But in the context of a season - and the recent evidence is in the book for this club - a relatively low-key victory in August is the foundation for wild nights beneath the lights in January and beyond.

On the two occasions Newcastle made the final of this competition under Eddie Howe, in 2023 and 2025, they also qualified for the Champions League. Momentum and feel-good have been by-products of progression.

Howe's successor, Matthias Jaissle, must have read the form guide. He named a strong XI and, when the first-half performance was not strong enough, he made the half-time change that turned the tie in his side's favour.

There days after the German intervened and brought on Joe Willock to score within a minute against Liverpool, Harvey Barnes did the same here, albeit with allowance for 60 seconds more. Decisive substitutions could well prove a hallmark of the new head coach. He certainly does not want for conviction in his own beliefs.

Harvey Barnes celebrates after firing Newcastle to a late victory over West Brom

Matthias Jaissle celebrates as Newcastle make the third round of the Carabao Cup

Barnes very quickly repaid his manager's faith in him being the game-changer when he followed up his own blocked shot to smash in at the Gallowgate End for 2-1. Then, at 2-2 with eight minutes to play, it was Barnes who met Amar Dedic's cross to sweep home the winner.

Jaissle's celebration was every bit as animated as those which greeted the goals during that 2-2 draw with Liverpool. It was the same when Ivorian winger Baz Toure cancelled out West Brom's opener with a close-range finish in the 38th minute. Man-of-the-match Dedic was again the provider.

As if to demonstrate further how serious he was taking this, Jaissle introduced three of his best players from Sunday's top-flight opener just after the hour. On came Yoane Wissa, Lewis Miley and Anthony Elanga to help protect a lead that never felt as safe as it perhaps should have done.

Credit to James Morrison's West Brom in that regard, for they played with adventure and purpose. Indeed, their 19th-minute lead was deserved. As midfielder Isaac Price sized a 25-yard free-kick, Newcastle goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen set a two-man wall.

He was expecting a cross to the far post, supported by his position in the middle of his goal. Price spotted the keeper's miscalculation and got his measurements just right, bending low around the under-staffed blockade and into the bottom corner.

With that, an edginess crept into St James' Park. Half an hour earlier, they had welcomed new £50million signing Nico Gonzalez onto the pitch. The former Manchester City midfielder seemed genuinely chuffed when a spontaneous chant of 'Nico, Nico, Nico' emanated from the Gallowgate End.

Isaac Price was at the double for West Brom and gave them a deserved lead in the 19th minute

Nico Gonzalez was paraded ahead of kick-off after completing his £50million move from Manchester City

He had, officially, only been a Newcastle player for 30 seconds when he was introduced.

His arrival, coupled with a team-sheet worth £365m, stirred a mood of buoyancy from the off, and those on the pitch responded. After Willock twice went close to scoring inside the opening seven minutes, it felt like being a stroll for Newcastle.

At least, that was, until West Brom started running forward with pace and directness.

And that is the challenge for Gonzalez. He has been bought to add elite-level experience to a midfield which, for all its young talent, needs an organiser and more resistance in there. That much was clear when the Championship side ran through to win a 76th-minute penalty converted by Price.

The apparent lottery of a penalty shootout awaited. Jaissle, though, had already gambled with substitutions of intent - and the reward, thanks to Barnes, was a place in the third round.

Only after the turn of the year might we see just how valuable this night really was for Jaissle and his new team.

Sports.title: 'He would have died for Everton': The aching sadness of Mike Lyons, the man who bled blue - and why his story should inspire David Moyes' side to go all out to win this season's League Cup
Sports.content:
'He would have died for Everton': The aching sadness of Mike Lyons, the man who bled blue - and why his story should inspire David Moyes' side to go all out to win this season's League Cup

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

A statistic currently going around about Everton being the only club among the Football League's 92 not to have won a trophy, a title or promotion, or been relegated, since the turn of the century has contributed to a pessimism which made a gathering of the club’s faithful last Friday evening very welcome.

The occasion, at the Denbigh Castle pub, a legendary gathering place for Evertonians in central Liverpool, celebrated the former Everton captain Mike Lyons, whose life and career have been charted in a fine new book.

The aching sadness underlying an occasion in which Lyons' former team-mates took turns to relate stories of the indefatigable, generous and hugely talented team-mate they knew and loved, is that the man in question is struggling now and could not be there.

His daughter Francesca, who lives near Liverpool and calls him every day at the care home in Perth, Australia, where he is living with dementia, reminds him how cherished he is among fans. Lyons, 74, knew that the event was taking place and he knows about the book, The Man Who Bled Blue, a meticulously researched and beautifully written biography by the journalist and author Simon Hart. But his brain has frayed terribly. His family and friends have helped Hart piece together the life story.

He would certainly empathise with those 21st century fans who yearn for silverware – any silverware – and not least the League Cup, which sends the team to Preston, David Moyes’ old club, on Wednesday night. Everton were reigning English champions, four days away from contesting a European Cup quarter-final, when Lyons made his debut in March 1971.

Mick Lyons made 473 appearances for Everton in his 12 years on Merseyside, scoring 59 goals

‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses’

With Everton team-mates Martin Dobson (left) and Bob Latchford (right)

Yet his 11 years as an Everton player did not yield him a single honour. Liverpool won 15 in that time. By 1982, Lyons was on his way to Sheffield Wednesday, missing by a couple of years the start of the glorious era when Everton won the FA Cup and two titles.

Had Lyons been at Friday’s event, talk would inevitably have turned to the League Cup – and his huge role in Everton's marathon against Aston Villa in the 1977 final, won by Villa in a second replay at Old Trafford. It remains one of the greatest clashes in the tournament's history and was the closest Lyons ever came to silverware with Everton.

Evertonians still remember the intensity of his celebration when he scored an equaliser in front of the Stretford End in the second replay. ‘Michael was more animated there than at any other goal he scored,’ his brother, Joe, tells Hart in the book. (To his family, Lyons has always been ‘Michael.’) Fatefully, he was then asked to push up as a utility centre-forward as Everton chased a winner – it’s a strategy still known as ‘Doing a Mike Lyons’ among Evertonians – and a hole materialised at the back which Villa exploited to score a late winner. In the seclusion of the car on the way home, Lyons wept.

This story teaches us, among other things, that barren times can produce some of the greatest heroes, like Lyons, and that the League Cup can bring such indelible memories that Everton, who have not always fielded strong teams in recent times, should see it as an opportunity.

Hart relates how, despite the initial Wembley final not yielding a winner, the team still appeared on a planned open-bus tour of Liverpool for which vast crowds turned out. The first replay, a thrilling 1-1 draw in Sheffield rescued by a late Bob Latchford goal, would remain one of Lyons’ favourite nights of his career. He later described the noise made by Evertonians that night as ‘something I’ll always treasure. It embodied everything I’ve always felt for this club’.

The biography’s title, alongside an image of Lyons with a gashed face as he leaves the pitch after Everton’s 1980 FA Cup semi-final against West Ham – another one they lost – captures his contribution. His myriad cuts, blows and collisions form a backdrop to the book. ‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses.’

The book’s beauty also resides in its small details, capturing the boundless enthusiasm and often comic innocence which accompanied Lyons' huge professionalism and work ethic.

He drove a club-issue Lada with his name emblazoned down the side. He eschewed the posh Liverpool hair salon which the players attended for their curly perms in favour of the work of team-mate Roger Kenyon’s wife Jackie, a hairdresser. Mrs Kenyon and Lyons’ wife Tricia were in such deep conversation in the Lyons’ kitchen that the perm solution was left in the Everton captain’s hair for too long. It was a catastrophe.

Shaking hands with Liverpool captain Emlyn Hughes ahead of the 1977 FA Cup semi-final at Maine Road

It is now 31 years since Everton last lifted a trophy, the 1995 FA Cup

The League Cup is the only major domestic trophy that Everton have never won, and it is time they rectified that point

You could have heard a pin drop in that Liverpool pub on Friday night when Francesca Lyons told the 100 or so people gathered that her father would have been humbled by all this attention. The consequences of his repeated heading of the ball are the same that so many old pros have had to face, full on, and Francesca has been an impressive advocate for football's need to do more for them.

There is a reason why the book’s subtitle is The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons. The Villa captain in the 1977 final was Chris Nicholl, who lived with the form of dementia caused by repeatedly heading footballs during his playing career, before he passed away in 2024.

But Friday evening was about the life-affirming qualities of a captain and player who, Francesca insisted, would not have had his life any other way. ‘He has always been so upbeat and fun,’ she said. ‘He would have probably laughed off all the attention because he’s always been so humble.’

Moyes, who also loves the bones of Everton, has a deep understanding of Lyons’ contribution. He and his long-time assistant Billy McKinlay paid him a visit during an Everton pre-season tour of Australia some time back. The League Cup remains a trophy Everton have never won. Lyons, who still watches the club’s games from Perth, would smile to see them finally lift the three-handled trophy next March, 50 years on from that legendary three-game marathon against Villa.

The Man Who Bled Blue: The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons by Simon Hart is published by Mount Vernon Publishing.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola worry dismissed as approach for winger is rebuffed
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola worry dismissed as approach for winger is rebuffed

Less than a week remains for Liverpool to bolster their attacking options

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola still wants to add two wingers to his Liverpool squad (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola has just days to transform Liverpool's attack before the summer transfer window slams shut. Iraola's era on the pitch, at least, officially began last Sunday, with the Reds drawing 2-2 to Newcastle United at St James' Park.

‌



All three of Liverpool's new signings featured in the clash. Jeremy Jacquet started, while Ronald Araujo and Victor Munoz came on in the second half. The trio all gave positive performances, but the Reds were noticeably lacking in midfield and in attack.

‌



Liverpool's forward line would certainly be bolstered by the arrival of Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola, who remains the club's top target this month. The Frenchman could be joined by Crystal Palace star Ismaila Sarr, following reports on Wednesday.

‌



Here, Mirror Football takes a look at all of the latest news coming out of Anfield as we tick closer to deadline day.

Sarr interest emerges

View 3 Images Ismaila Sarr is a target for Liverpool (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Liverpool's pursuit of attackers has been one of the stories of the transfer window. A move for Bradley Barcola is still on the cards, although their short-lived pursuit of Brighton & Hove Albion star Yankuba Minteh appears to be just that, short-lived.

‌



It now seems as though the Reds have turned their attentions to Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr. According to The Athletic, the Reds have had initial approach for the 28-year-old turned down.

Sarr is well-known to Liverpool – and not only for his exploits for Watford and Palace. He was placed on three-man shortlist in the summer of 2020 during his days at Vicarage Road. Although they now appear to have resurrected that interest, it would seem only an astronomical offer would tempt Palace to sell.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Alejandro Balde decision made and star 'expects to leave' in next week
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Alejandro Balde decision made and star 'expects to leave' in next week

Manchester United continue to work on both new signings and potential sales as the September 1 transfer deadline draws nearer

View 2 Images Alejandre Balde has reportedly reached a decision on his future and informed Barcelona of his intentions (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester United are hard at work burning the candle at both ends as they work on an array of potential transfer business. Less than a week of the summer window remains for the club to do business, with more deals expected through both the arrivals and departure gates.

‌



Michael Carrick may be even more convinced his squad needs new additions following Saturday's humbling 2-0 defeat at Hull City. The Red Devils face another Premier League newcomer in Ipswich on Sunday, with the alarm bells set to ring if that fixture results in anything but three points.

‌



United will be working frantically to get business over the line but need to be increasingly hasty in negotiations. Mirror Football collects all the latest murmurs from around Old Trafford today as the club enters a crucial period in the calendar.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Balde tells Barca he wants to stay

United may have to keep their options alive in the hunt for a new left-back after Alejandro Balde reportedly told Barcelona he wants to stay. Reports linking the Spain defender with a move to Old Trafford had escalated this week after Balde was omitted from Barca's season-opening win over Elche.

Man Utd face major Alejandro Balde transfer issue as they search for Lewis Hall alternative READ MORE :

That only fuelled rumours suggesting an offer from United was imminent. The Premier League giants would prefer a loan deal with an option to buy the player, only for it to emerge Los Cules were only interested in a direct sale.

‌



However, Fabrizio Romano has now reported Balde's decision to tell Barcelona he wishes to stay put. That's despite the increase in competition caused by Xavi Espart's emergence as a new option and Joao Cancelo's summer return to the Camp Nou.

La Masia graduate Espart impressed at left-back against Elche and grabbed an assist for his troubles. Hansi Flick said after the game that he would have to speak to Balde on Monday after deciding he wasn't mentally prepared to play - and that chat appears to have been a positive one from Barca's perspective.

‌



Reports had suggested United would need to pay around £30million to sign the 22-year-old, who is seen as an alternative to the much more expensive Lewis Hall. However, Romano has said it would now require a "big proposal" to get him out of Catalonia this summer.

Zirkzee 'expects to leave'

The Daily Mail has reported Joshua Zirkzee expects to leave United between now and the September 1 deadline. The Dutchman has been tipped for an exit for much of the summer thus far and could find a willing suitor in Juventus.

Juve would be even better-equipped to chase his signature if they manage to offload Jonathan David in the coming days. And Romano has said on his YouTube channel that could be possible after Atletico Madrid showed interest in the Canadian forward.

Sports.title: Chelsea's dream end to transfer window as Alex Scott signs and £270million stars sold
Sports.content:
Chelsea's dream end to transfer window as Alex Scott signs and £270million stars sold

Chelsea have been busy in the transfer market this summer, but with the window still open, here's what an ideal ending could look like for the Blues

View 4 Images It looks set to be a busy week for Chelsea and Xabi Alonso (Image: Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images)

It has been a rollercoaster of a summer for Chelsea - and there may still be a few big loops left before the transfer window closes. Having already spent roughly £350million on nine new arrivals - headlined by a club-record £117m move for Morgan Rogers - the focus in SW6 has shifted abruptly from buying to selling.

‌



With 39 senior players currently listed in their squad, Chelsea sit well over the Premier League's 25-man registration cap. Trimming it before the September 1 deadline is a substantial task, but the club's track record as sharp, effective sellers should keep panic at bay.

‌



A late push from Manchester City for Enzo Fernandez could still force Chelsea back into the market for a replacement midfielder and after Robert Sanchez's horror show on Monday, the urge to bring in a new goalkeeper has become impossible to ignore.

‌



With that in mind, here's what a dream end to the transfer window might look like for Xabi Alonso's Blues.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chelsea ask fans to stop controversial chant after loud Fulham rendition READ MORE :

Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and laughing gas possession after motorway crash READ MORE :

Signing Alex Scott

If Fernandez leaves, Chelsea will need a top-class, Premier League-proven midfielder with a high ceiling to take his place - and Alex Scott fits the bill perfectly. The Blues have reportedly already seen three bids knocked back by Bournemouth, who remain adamant the 23-year-old is off-limits. But every stand has its price, and an offer of around £80m would be hard for the Cherries to turn down.

‌



Financially and strategically, it's a move where everyone wins. Should Fernandez force his way to Manchester City for £120-£130m, replacing a player who no longer wants to be at Stamford Bridge with Scott for £80m would leave Chelsea with a Premier League-ready replacement and a tidy £40-£50m in net profit.

Tactically, Scott is tailor-made for Alonso's high-octane system. Naturally press-resistant, he has an uncanny knack for absorbing pressure, riding tackles, and carrying the ball through compact lines. Combined with his defensive hustle and quick-release passing, Scott would give Chelsea the ideal mix of control, grit, and forward momentum.

View 4 Images Alex Scott would be the ideal replacement for Enzo Fernandez (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

‌



£270m in player sales

The Fernandez saga might be getting all the headlines, but clearing out the deadwood must be Chelsea's primary focus this week. If done right, the Blues could potentially pocket upwards of £270m.

Liam Delap is reportedly on the verge of joining Nottingham Forest for £45m, with a further £5m in add-ons, while Aston Villa are in advanced talks to sign Nicolas Jackson for £65m. In an ideal scenario, both of those deals go through without incident. But Chelsea don't stop there.

They then sell young forward Marc Guiu for around £15m and outcast defender Tosin Adarabioyo for roughly the same. This, as well as fees secured from loan exits of the likes of Mykhalio Mudryk, Mamadou Sarr and Aaron Anselmino, could see the Blues pocket over £150m before the window closes.

‌



And with City well aware that only a sum of £120m will do for Fernandez, the total could reach a staggering figure that offsets the earlier summer outlay.

View 4 Images The sales of Nicolas Jackson and Liam Delap could see Chelsea pocket over £100m

Replace Robert Sanchez

Chelsea's goalkeeping situation is a lot trickier than it might seem at first glance. While Sanchez's recurring errors make upgrading a priority, spending big on a permanent fixture risks blocking a pathway for Mike Penders.

‌



The 6ft 7in Belgian - already drawing comparisons to Thibaut Courtois - looks primed for senior football and if Chelsea's internal assessment is right, their long-term solution between the sticks is already on their books.

Splashing £60-£70m on a shiny new No. 1 brings two distinct dangers. First, it could drive Penders out of the club - a painful echo of how Chelsea previously squeezed out fellow Belgians Kevin De Bruyne and Romelu Lukaku, only to watch fall into enemy hands years later. Second, there's the lingering caution of the Kepa Arrizabalaga saga: the real possibility of dropping astronomical money on a marquee signing who fails to deliver.

View 4 Images Chelsea either need to put their faith in Mike Penders or find a solution that suits both him and the club (Image: Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



That leaves Chelsea with two options: throw Penders straight into the deep end and have him replace Sanchez as the club's No. 1, or sign a temporary fixture to bridge the gap.

According to The Athletic, the Blues are in talks to sign Aston Villa's Emi Martinez, who could be the perfect compromise - not to sign outright, but rather to bring in on loan.

While Villa would prefer to sell Martinez - particularly after signing Zion Suzuki - Chelsea could test the waters by offering a hefty loan fee - say, £10m. Ideally, they'd then loan Penders out to a Premier League club, with Sanchez relegated to Chelsea's No. 2 for the season.

Article continues below

This scenario would give the Blues an elite goalkeeper immediately, but would also buy Penders a full season of breathing room without blocking his path long-term. If, in a year, Penders has proven himself, he can come back and take over the gloves from Martinez. If not, Chelsea can look elsewhere without the fear of allowing a real gem to slip through their grasp.
